On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So he [the hoopoe] did not remain long, and said: "I have comprehended [knowledge of] what you have not comprehended, and I have come to you from Sheba with certain news."﴾ (22)

He, exalted is He, means by His words ﴿So he did not remain long﴾: Solomon remained not long from the time he asked about the hoopoe until the hoopoe came.

The reciters differed over the reading of His words ﴿fa-makatha﴾ (فَمَكَثَ). The majority of the reciters of the cities, apart from ʿĀṣim, read it as "fa-makuṯa" (فَمَكُثَ) with a ḍamma on the kāf, while ʿĀṣim read it with a fatḥa. Both readings are correct in our view, since they are two well-known dialects (lughatān), though the ḍamma is more pleasing to me, because it is the more famous and eloquent of the two.

* *

As for His words ﴿He said: "I have comprehended [knowledge of] what you have not comprehended"﴾:

He says: the hoopoe said, when Solomon asked him about his absence and his lateness: "I have comprehended knowledge of what you, O Solomon, have not comprehended."

As related:

- Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿I have comprehended [what you have not comprehended]﴾: "[It means] what you do not know."

- Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Salama related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, regarding ﴿So he did not remain long﴾: then the hoopoe came, and Solomon said to him: "What kept you from your turn?" He said: "I have comprehended what you have not comprehended."

* *

As for His words ﴿and I have come to you from Sheba with certain news﴾:

He says: "I have come to you from Sheba with true, certain news."

And this is what has been related:

- Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Salama related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, regarding ﴿and I have come to you from Sheba with certain news﴾: that is, "I have reached a kingdom which your kingdom has not reached."

The reciters differed over the reading of His words ﴿min Sabaʾin﴾ (مِنْ سَبَإٍ). The majority of the reciters of Madina and Kufa read it ﴿min Sabaʾin﴾ with tanwīn (with inflection), meaning that it is a man named Sabaʾ. Some reciters of Makka and Basra read it ﴿min Sabaʾa﴾ without inflection, taking it as the name of a tribe or of a woman.

The correct position on this is to say: both are well-known readings, and scholars among the reciters have read each of them; whichever of them the reader recites is correct. So inflecting Sabaʾ and not inflecting it are both correct, because if Sabaʾ is a man, as the report indicates, then when the man is meant it is inflected, and if the tribe is meant it is not inflected. As the poet said, inflecting it:

*al-wāridūna wa-Taymun fī dharā Sabaʾin*
*qad ʿaḍḍa aʿnāqahum jildu l-jawāmīsi*

(Narrated by the author once before in this work, and it is one of al-Farrāʾ's witnesses in his Maʿānī l-Qurʾān.) The author cites it here a second time, to show that if "Sabaʾ" is the name of a tribe of Yemen, it is diptotic (ghayr munṣarif) on account of being a proper noun and feminine; if its origin is considered, namely that it is the name of the tribe's ancestor, then it is masculine and inflected.

It is related with the variants dharā and dhurā. I was told, from al-Farrāʾ, from al-Ruʾāsī, that he asked Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ why Sabaʾ is not inflected. He said: "I do not know what it is." So Abū ʿAmr left it uninflected because he did not know what it was, just as the Arabs leave unknown names uninflected when they do not recognise them; it is related of some of them: "This is Abū Maʿrūr has come," leaving it uninflected because they did not recognise it among their names. The commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Why do they not prostrate to Allah, who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth, and knows what you conceal and what you disclose? (25) Allah — there is no deity except Him, the Lord of the Mighty Throne.﴾ (26)

The readers differed over the recitation of His words ﴿Why do they not prostrate to Allah﴾. Some Meccan readers, some Medinan readers and the Kufan readers read "ألا" (alā) with a light pronunciation (takhfīf), meaning: "Alā yā hā'ulā'i, usjudū" (Oh, you people, prostrate!), so they omitted "hā'ulā'" (these people), relying on the indication of "yā" (O) for it. Some of them reported from the Arabs by hearing: "Alā yā irḥamnā" (Oh, have mercy on us!), "Alā yā taṣaddaq 'alaynā" (Oh, give charity to us!). He also cited the verse of al-Akhtal:

"Alā yā aslamī yā Hinda Hinda Banī Badr ... wa in kāna ḥayyānā 'ida ākhira al-dahr"

[[The verse: it is attributed in (Lisan al-Arab, under "ʿadā") to al-Akhtal al-Taghlibi, the Umayyad poet. He said: "The word ʿidā has come in poetry meaning enemies." Ibn al-A'rabi, regarding al-Akhtal's words "Alā yā aslamī..." the verse: "ʿidā" means distance. And "qawm ʿidā" means people who are distant, with no kinship or alliance between them; and "qawm ʿidā" means people at war. The verse has been transmitted with both kasra and damma, like "sawā" and "sawā". Al-Asma'i said: It is said: "hā'ulā'i qawmun ʿidan" (with a short final vowel), which is used for enemies and strangers. "Qawm ʿidā" (with damma on the ʿayn) is not said unless the hā' is added, so you say "ʿadāh," on the pattern of "quḍāh." Abu Zayd said: "Ṭālat ʿadawā'uhum," meaning their distance and dispersion. The author's evidence in this verse: the vocative particle yā enters upon an omitted vocative noun. Its estimate: "Alā yā hādhihi aslamī." This is analogous to the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Alā yā usjudū", its estimate: "Alā yā hā'ulā'i usjudū." So "hā'ulā'" was omitted, relying on the indication of "yā" for it.]]

On this reading, "usjudū" in this position is jussive, and "alā" has no place in the i'rab (grammatical analysis). Most of the readers of Medina, Kufa and Basra read ﴿Alla yasjudū﴾ with a heavy pronunciation of "alla" (an-lā, "so that not"), meaning: "And Satan made their deeds appealing to them, so that they would not prostrate to Allah." "Alla" is in the accusative position, for the reason I mentioned, that its meaning is "li-allā" (so that not), and "yasjudū" is in the accusative position after "an."

The correct view on this matter is that both are recitations widely transmitted among the reciters of the cities, and scholars among the readers have recited each of them, with both meanings being sound.

The people of Arabic grammar differed over the way "yā" enters in the recitation of one who read it in the imperative form. Some grammarians of Basra said: whoever recites it thus, it is as if he made it an imperative, as if he said to them, "usjudū" (prostrate!), and he added "yā" between them, which indicates an alert, then the alif of the wasl (connection) in "usjudū" was dropped, and the alif in "yā" was dropped, because it was a sukūn (unvocalized) meeting the sīn, so it became "alā yasjudū." Some grammarians of Kufa said: this "yā" that enters for the vocative is sufficient without the noun, and the noun is sufficient without it; so you say "yā aqbil" (O, come forward!) and "Zayd aqbil" (Zayd, come forward!), and whatever fell of the unvocalized letters is on this basis.

By His words ﴿yukhrij al-khabʾ﴾ (brings forth what is hidden) he means: He brings out what is hidden in the heavens and the earth, such as rain from the sky, plants from the earth, and the like.

Those who interpreted it said the same as what we have said, though their expressions differed about it.

Those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, a reading from Mujahid: ﴿yukhrij al-khabʾ fī al-samāwāt﴾, he said: "The rain."

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najīḥ, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿yukhrij al-khabʾ﴾, he said: "The rain."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿alladhī yukhrij al-khabʾ fī al-samāwāti wa al-arḍ﴾: "The hidden thing of the heavens and the earth is what Allah placed in them of provisions: the rain from the sky, and the plants from the earth. They were a joined mass, the one not raining and the other not growing; so He split the sky, sent down rain from it, and brought forth plants."

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abi Khālid, from Ḥakīm ibn Jābir, regarding His words ﴿Alla yasjudū li-llāhi alladhī yukhrij al-khabʾ fī al-samāwāti wa al-arḍ﴾: "And He knows every secret thing in the heavens and the earth."

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmmāra narrated to me, saying: ʿUbayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Usama ibn Zayd informed us, from Muʿādh ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: I saw Ibn ʿAbbas on a mule asking Tubaʿ, the son of Ka'b's wife: "Did you ask Ka'b about the seed: does the earth grow it in the year when the other year does not receive rain?" He said: "I heard Ka'b say: The seed descends from the sky and comes forth from the earth." He said: "You have spoken the truth."

Abu Jaʿfar said: It is "Tubaʿ," but Muhammad said it thus. It was also said: "yukhrij al-khabʾ fī al-samāwāt wa al-arḍ," because the Arabs put "min" in place of "fī" and "fī" in place of "min" in the sense of extraction.

His words ﴿wa yaʿlamu mā tukhfūna wa mā tuʿlinūn﴾ mean: He knows the secret of the affairs of His creation, these whom Satan made their deeds appealing to, and their open matters. This is on the reading of one who reads "alla" with the heavy pronunciation. As for the reading of one who reads it with the light pronunciation, its meaning is: He knows what His creatures conceal, whom He commanded to prostrate by His words, "Alā yā hā'ulā'i usjudū." It has been mentioned that in the reading of Ubayy it is: "Alā tasjudū li-llāhi alladhī yaʿlamu sirrakum wa mā tuʿlinūn."

And His words: ﴿Allah, there is no deity except Him﴾

He, may He be exalted, says: Allah, the One for whom worship is alone fitting, there is no deity except Him, there is no object of worship other than Him for whom worship is fitting. So sincerely worship Him, single Him out with obedience, and do not associate anything with Him. ﴿Lord of the Mighty Throne﴾: by this he means: the Owner of the Mighty Throne, which every throne, however great, is beneath; no throne resembles it, neither the throne of the Queen of Sheba nor any other.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿I have encompassed what you have not encompassed﴾ up to His words ﴿There is no deity except Him, Lord of the Mighty Throne﴾: "All of this is the speech of the hoopoe."

⁕ Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, in similar terms.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verses 27–28:

The exegesis of His words, exalted is He: ﴿He said: "We shall see whether you have told the truth or whether you have been of the liars. Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them; then withdraw from them and see what they return."﴾

His words, may His remembrance be exalted, mean: Solomon said to the hoopoe, ﴿"We shall see"﴾ regarding the excuse you have offered and the argument you have advanced for your absence from us, and regarding the news you have brought us, ﴿"whether you have told the truth"﴾ in all of that, ﴿"or whether you have been of the liars" in it. "Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them; then withdraw from them and see what they return."﴾

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the interpretation of this. Some of them said: its meaning is: "Take this letter of mine, deliver it to them, and see what they return; then withdraw from them, turning back to me." He said: this is of the delayed (al-mu'akhkhar) which means the advanced (al-taqdim).

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Solomon answered him, meaning the hoopoe answered when he had finished: ﴿"We shall see whether you have told the truth or whether you have been of the liars. Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them"﴾ and see what they return, then withdraw from them, turning back to me. He said: There was a window facing the sun, and at the hour the sun rises, it would rise through it and prostrate to it. The hoopoe came and landed in it and blocked it, and the sun was delayed, so she stood to look, and he threw the letter to her from under his wing, and flew off until she stood looking at the sun.

Abu Ja'far said: This statement of Ibn Zayd indicates that the hoopoe turned back to Solomon after casting the letter, and that her looking at the sun was before she received Solomon's letter, and what she did in turning back.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them, then withdraw from them, and be near them, and see what they return." They said: the hoopoe did so, and heard the queen's consultation with the people of her realm, and her words to them: ﴿"Indeed, a noble letter has been delivered to me. Indeed, it is from Solomon, and indeed it reads: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate"﴾ and what followed of their consulting one another.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, his statement: ﴿"deliver it to them, then withdraw from them"﴾, i.e., be near, ﴿"and see what they return"﴾. And this view is more similar to the interpretation of the verse, because the queen's consulting her people occurred after the letter had been delivered to her, and the hoopoe would not have departed when he had been commanded to watch the people's consultation among themselves, what they discuss, before doing what Solomon commanded him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verses 27–28:

The exegesis of His words, exalted is He: ﴿He said: "We shall see whether you have told the truth or whether you have been of the liars. Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them; then withdraw from them and see what they return."﴾

His words, may His remembrance be exalted, mean: Solomon said to the hoopoe, ﴿"We shall see"﴾ regarding the excuse you have offered and the argument you have advanced for your absence from us, and regarding the news you have brought us, ﴿"whether you have told the truth"﴾ in all of that, ﴿"or whether you have been of the liars" in it. "Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them; then withdraw from them and see what they return."﴾

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the interpretation of this. Some of them said: its meaning is: "Take this letter of mine, deliver it to them, and see what they return; then withdraw from them, turning back to me." He said: this is of the delayed (al-mu'akhkhar) which means the advanced (al-taqdim).

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Solomon answered him, meaning the hoopoe answered when he had finished: ﴿"We shall see whether you have told the truth or whether you have been of the liars. Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them"﴾ and see what they return, then withdraw from them, turning back to me. He said: There was a window facing the sun, and at the hour the sun rises, it would rise through it and prostrate to it. The hoopoe came and landed in it and blocked it, and the sun was delayed, so she stood to look, and he threw the letter to her from under his wing, and flew off until she stood looking at the sun.

Abu Ja'far said: This statement of Ibn Zayd indicates that the hoopoe turned back to Solomon after casting the letter, and that her looking at the sun was before she received Solomon's letter, and what she did in turning back.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them, then withdraw from them, and be near them, and see what they return." They said: the hoopoe did so, and heard the queen's consultation with the people of her realm, and her words to them: ﴿"Indeed, a noble letter has been delivered to me. Indeed, it is from Solomon, and indeed it reads: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate"﴾ and what followed of their consulting one another.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, his statement: ﴿"deliver it to them, then withdraw from them"﴾, i.e., be near, ﴿"and see what they return"﴾. And this view is more similar to the interpretation of the verse, because the queen's consulting her people occurred after the letter had been delivered to her, and the hoopoe would not have departed when he had been commanded to watch the people's consultation among themselves, what they discuss, before doing what Solomon commanded him.

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: "She said: O chiefs, indeed there has been delivered to me a noble letter (29). Indeed it is from Solomon, and indeed it reads: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful (30). Do not be haughty toward me, and come to me in submission (31)."

His words, may His remembrance be exalted, mean: So the hoopoe (al-hudhud) took Solomon's letter to her, delivered it to her, and when she read it she said to her people: "O chiefs, indeed there has been delivered to me a noble letter."

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Solomon ibn Dawud wrote with the hoopoe: "In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. From Solomon ibn Dawud, to Bilqis daughter of Dhu Sarh and her people. As to what follows: do not be haughty toward me, and come to me in submission." He said: So the hoopoe took the letter in its leg, set off with it until it reached her. She had a window in her house, and when the sun rose she would look at it and prostrate to it. The hoopoe came to the window and blocked it with its wings until the sun had risen and she did not notice. Then it dropped the letter through the window, and it fell upon her in the place where she was, and she took it.

* al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Abu Sufyan related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: It has reached me that she was a woman called Bilqis, I think he said: daughter of Sharahil, one of whose parents was from the jinn, and the back of one of her feet was like the hoof of a beast. She was in a house of kingship, and her counsellors were three hundred and twelve, each man of them over ten thousand. She was in a land called Ma'rib, three days from San'a. When the hoopoe brought news of her to Solomon ibn Dawud, he wrote the letter and sent it with the hoopoe. The hoopoe came when the doors had been locked, and she used to lock her doors and place her keys under her head. The hoopoe entered through a window and dropped the page upon her. She read it, and in it was: "Indeed it is from Solomon, and indeed it reads: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Do not be haughty toward me, and come to me in submission." Thus were the prophets accustomed to write: they did not elaborate, but wrote in short phrases.

* He said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Solomon added nothing to what God related in His book: "indeed it is from Solomon, and indeed it reads."

* I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: "Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them" (27:28): So the hoopoe went off with the letter until, when it came level with the queen while she was on her throne, it dropped the letter to her.

* * *

As for His words: "She said: O chiefs, indeed there has been delivered to me a noble letter."

Al-mala' (the chiefs) are the nobles of her people. The meaning, as His remembrance is exalted: the queen of Sheba said to the nobles of her people: "O chiefs, indeed there has been delivered to me a noble letter."

The people of knowledge differed over the reason she described the letter as noble. Some said she described it so because it was sealed. 

Others said she described it so because it came from a king, and so she described it as noble for the nobility of its sender. Among those who said this was Ibn Zayd.

* Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: "indeed there has been delivered to me a noble letter": It is the letter of Solomon, when he wrote to her.

* * *

As for His words: "Indeed it is from Solomon, and indeed it reads: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful."

The first and second "inna" are read with a kasra as a resumption (radd) upon the "inni" in His words: "indeed there has been delivered to me a noble letter." The meaning of the speech: she said: "O chiefs, indeed there has been delivered to me a letter, and indeed it is from Solomon."

* * *

As for His words: "Do not be haughty toward me, and come to me in submission."

He says: a noble letter was delivered to me: "do not be haughty toward me."

There are two grammatical possibilities for "an" (that): if it is taken as an apposition (badal) to "the letter," it is in the nominative case, following the case of the letter it is apposed to; and if the meaning of the speech is taken as: "indeed there has been delivered to me a noble letter, that do not be haughty toward me," then it is in the accusative, the letter being governed by it.

By His words: "do not be haughty toward me" is meant: do not be arrogant or self-important regarding what I have invited you to.

As:

* Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: "do not be haughty toward me": do not refuse what I have invited you to; if you refuse, I will wage war against you. I said to Ibn Zayd: "do not be haughty toward me" means do not be arrogant toward me? He said: Yes. And Ibn Zayd said: "Do not be haughty toward me, and come to me in submission" — that is in Solomon's letter to her.

* * *

As for His words: "and come to me in submission."

He says: come to me submitting to Allah in His oneness and obedience.

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: "She said: O chiefs, indeed there has been delivered to me a noble letter (29). **Commentary on the words of the Exalted: ﴿She said, "O chiefs, advise me concerning my affair. I do not decide any matter until you bear witness."﴾ (32) ﴿They said, "We are possessors of strength and possessors of great might, but the command is yours, so consider what you will command."﴾ (33)**

God, may He be remembered, says: The Queen of Sheba said to the nobles of her people: ﴿O chiefs, advise me concerning my affair.﴾ She means: Give me your counsel regarding my matter, which has come before me concerning the owner of this letter that was delivered to me. She made the consultation a request for a legal opinion (fatwa).

* *

And His saying: ﴿I do not decide any matter until you bear witness.﴾

She means: I would not settle any matter in this regard until you witness it, so that I may consult you about it.

As related:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: She summoned her people to consult them: ﴿O chiefs, advise me concerning my affair. I do not decide any matter until you bear witness.﴾ He says, in the sense of the speech: "I would not decide a matter without you, nor would I issue a ruling on a matter." Therefore she said: ﴿I do not decide any matter﴾, meaning: "deciding" (qadiya).

* *

And His saying: ﴿They said, "We are possessors of strength and possessors of great might."﴾

God, may He be remembered, says: The nobles of the Queen of Sheba's people said, when she consulted them about her affair and the affair of Solomon: "We are those who possess strength for fighting, and great might in war. The command is yours, O Queen, regarding fighting and regarding abandoning it. So consider what opinion you see, and order us, and we will carry out your command."

Those who expounded the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) said what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿They said, "We are possessors of strength and possessors of great might"﴾ — they offered her battle; they would fight on her behalf. ﴿The command is yours after this, so consider what you will command.﴾

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, who said: With the Queen of Sheba were twelve thousand *qayl*s [[al-qayl, with a fatha on the qaf and sukun after it, means a minor king in Yemen; its plural is aqyal and quyul. As for quyul, perhaps with a fatha on the qaf, meaning a single king, I have not found it in the lexicons; it may be a general term used among the Yemenis.]], with each *qayl* having a hundred thousand.

Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: With Bilqis were a hundred thousand *qayl*s, with each *qayl* a hundred thousand.

He said: Waki' narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, saying: I heard Mujahid say: Under the authority of the Queen of Sheba were twelve thousand *quyul*, and *quyul* in their language means a king; under the authority of each king were a hundred thousand fighting men.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verse 34:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿She said: Indeed, kings, when they enter a city, ruin it and make the honored of its people humiliated. And thus do they act.﴾

His words, exalted is He, mean: the queen of Sheba said to the chiefs of her people, when they offered her themselves for fighting Solomon, if she should order them to do so: ﴿Indeed, kings, when they enter a city﴾ by force and conquest, ﴿ruin it﴾, meaning: they devastate it, ﴿and make the honored of its people humiliated﴾, and that is by enslaving the free and reducing them to bondage. Her statement about kings was reported in this place, and then God said: ﴿And thus do they act﴾, meaning, exalted is He: just as the queen of Sheba said, so do kings act when they enter a city by force.

Similar to what we have said regarding this, the people of ta'wil (interpretation) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Abu Bakr narrated to us, regarding His words: ﴿and make the honored of its people humiliated﴾, he said: Abu Bakr said: this is by force.

- Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, he said: Abu Bakr narrated to us, he said: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Muslim, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, kings, when they enter a city, ruin it﴾, he said: when they enter it by force, they devastate it.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿She said: Indeed, kings, when they enter a city, ruin it and make the honored of its people humiliated﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: God says: ﴿And thus do they act﴾.

Commentary on the verse of the Qur'an, "Indeed, I am going to send them a gift and see with what the messengers will return" (27:35) to "...and We will surely expel them from it in humiliation, and they will be debased" (27:37)

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: "And indeed, I will send them a gift and see with what the messengers return" (27:35), "So when he came to Solomon, he said, 'Do you provide me with wealth? But what Allah has given me is better than what He has given you. Rather, it is you who rejoice in your gift.'" (27:36) "Return to them, for we will surely come to them with soldiers they cannot resist, and we will surely expel them from it in humiliation, and they will be debased." (27:37)

She had been governed and had governed until that sharpened her; and her religion and the religion of her people, as it is mentioned, was Zandaqa (heresy). When she read the letter, she heard a document unlike the letters of the kings who had been before her. So she sent to the notables of Yemen and said to them: "O chiefs, indeed there has been delivered to me a noble letter. Indeed it is from Solomon, and indeed it is: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Do not exalt yourselves over me, and come to me in submission." Up to His saying: "with what the messengers return." Then she said: "A letter has come to me the like of which has not come to me from any king before him. If this man is a prophet sent, we have no power or strength against him; and if he is a king who seeks to outdo us, he is no mightier than us and no more numerous." So she prepared gifts of the kind given to kings, by which they are tempted, and said: "If he is a king, he will accept the gift and desire wealth; and if he is a prophet, he has no need of the world, and it is not that he seeks, but he wants us to enter his religion and follow his command," or as she said.

Al-Husayn narrated, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: "And indeed, I am sending to them a gift": "She sent female servants and male servants, dressed in one kind of clothing. She said: 'If he separates them so that the male is distinguished from the female, then return the gift, for he is a prophet; we should follow him and enter his religion.' So Solomon separated the boys from the girls and returned the gift, and said: 'Do you provide me with wealth? But what Allah has given me is better than what He has given you.'"

Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said: Among the gifts she sent were female servants and male servants who wore different clothing, so that the boys could be distinguished from the girls. He said: Then he called for water, and the girls began washing from the elbow downward, and the boys washed from the elbow upward. He said: My father used to narrate this report to us.

'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, who said: Marwan ibn Mu'awiya narrated to us, who said: Isma'il narrated to us, from Abu Salih: "And indeed, I am sending to them a gift." He said: "She sent a brick of gold, and said: 'If he desires the world, I will know it; and if he desires the Hereafter, I will know it.'"

* *

As for His saying: "and will see with what the messengers return"

You say: I will look at what news and action of his regarding my gift which I send to him will cause my messengers to return: with acceptance and departure from us, or with rejection of the gift and insistence on demanding that they follow him in his religion? The alif was dropped from "ma" in His saying "bi-m" (with what), and its origin is "bi-ma", because when the Arabs use "ma" with the meaning of "ayy" (which) and then join it to a preposition, they drop its alif to distinguish the interrogative from other uses, as His majestic praise said: "About what do they question one another?" (78:1) and "They said: 'In what were you?'" (74:42). Sometimes they retain the alif in it, as the poet said:

"'Alamā qāma yashtumunī la'īmun... ka-khinzīrin tamarragha fī turāb"
[The verse is by Hassan ibn Thabit and is among the witnesses in the book al-Mughni of Ibn Hisham, where "ma" appears with two other variants in its rhyme (fī dimān, fī ramād). Ibn Hisham said: The alif of the interrogative "ma" must be dropped when it is preceded by a preposition, leaving the fatha as evidence of it, such as fīm, ilām, 'alām, and bim; the reason for dropping the alif is to distinguish the interrogative from the declarative, so it is dropped in such cases as (fīm anta min dhikrāhā), (fa-nāzirah bim yarji'u al-mursalūn), (lima taqūlūna mā lā taf'alūn). As for the reading of 'Ikrimah and 'Isa "('amma yatasā'alūn)", it is rare; and as for Hassan's "'alā mā qāma" verse, it is a poetic necessity, and "al-dimān" is like "al-ramād" in weight and meaning. It is also transmitted as "fī ramād", so I preferred it over Ibn al-Shajari's interpretation of it as "dung"; and similar to it is the other's saying: "Indeed we have killed your chiefs for our slain, the people of the banner, so what does the talk become abundant about?"]
This comprises the meaning of the author's remark on this witness.

She said: "Indeed, I am sending to them" — she sent only to Solomon alone, in the manner we explained in His saying: "upon fear from Pharaoh and his chiefs" (10:83), and His saying: "So when he came to Solomon, he said, 'Do you provide me with wealth?'"

If someone says: How is it said "So when he came to Solomon," making the report about the coming of Solomon refer to one person, while earlier it says "and will see with what the messengers return"? If the messenger was one, how is it said "with what the messengers return," and if they were a group, how is it said "So when he came to Solomon"? It is said: This is similar to what we have already explained about the Arabs expressing a report about a matter that came from one person in the form of a report about a group, when the intention is not a report about one specific person pointed out individually; so it is mentioned in the report. It has also been said that the messenger whom the queen of Sheba sent to Solomon was a single man, and therefore it says: "So when he came to Solomon," meaning: when the messenger came to Solomon. Those who held this view supported its correctness by Solomon's saying to the messenger: "Return to them," and it is mentioned that in the reading of 'Abd Allah it is "fa-lamma jā'ū Sulaymān" in the plural, corresponding to the wording "with what the messengers return," so the plural suits the wording and the singular suits the meaning.

* *

As for His saying: "Do you provide me with wealth?"

He says: Solomon said, when the messenger came from the woman with her gifts: "Do you provide me with wealth?"

The readers differed in reading this. Some readers of Medina read "Atumiddūnani" with two nūns and the yā' retained. Some Kufans read it similarly, except that they omitted the yā' at the end and vocalized the final nūn with kasra. Some Basran readers read it with two nūns, retaining the yā' in connected speech and omitting it in pause. Some Kufan readers read it with a doubled nūn and the yā' retained. All these readings are close to one another, and all are correct, because they are known in the dialects of the Arabs and famous in their speech.

* *

As for His saying: "But what Allah has given me is better than what He has given you"

He says: What Allah has given me of wealth and the world is greater than and superior to what He has given you of it. "Rather, it is you who rejoice in your gift" — he says: I do not rejoice in your gift which you sent to me; rather, you rejoice in the gift that is sent to you, because you are people who boast of the world and vie with one another for it; the world and its wealth are not among my needs, because God, may His remembrance be exalted, has empowered me over it and made me king over it in a way He has not made any other king.

"Return to them": this is Solomon's speech to the woman's messenger: "Return to them, for we will surely come to them with soldiers they cannot resist," meaning: they have no power to face them and no ability to repel them from what they wish of them.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some of the people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When the gifts came to Solomon, including the female servants and male servants, the pure-bred horses, and kinds of worldly goods, he said to the messengers who had brought it: "Do you provide me with wealth? But what Allah has given me is better than what He has given you. Rather, it is you who rejoice in your gift," because I have no need of your gift, and my view of it is not like your view; so return to her with what you have brought from her. "Then we will surely come to them with soldiers they cannot resist."

'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, who said: Marwan ibn Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying: "Then we will surely come to them with soldiers they cannot resist," he said: "They have no power to face them."

* *

As for His saying: "And We will surely expel them from it in humiliation, and they will be debased"

He says: And we will surely expel those who sent you from their land in humiliation, and they will be debased, if they do not come to me in submission.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some of the people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: "And We will surely expel them from it in humiliation, and they will be debased," or they will come to me in submission, they and their people.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verses 38–40 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿He said: "O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?" (38) An ifrit of the jinn said: "I will bring it to you before you rise from your place. Indeed, I am strong and trustworthy for it." (39) He said, the one who had knowledge of the Scripture: "I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you." And when he saw it settled in his presence, he said: "This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful, his gratitude is only for himself; and whoever is ungrateful, indeed my Lord is Free of need and Generous." (40)﴾

The scholars differed concerning the time at which Sulayman said: ﴿O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne?﴾ Some of them said: He said that when the hoopoe (al-hudhud) brought him the news of the Queen of Sheba, and said to him: ﴿And I have come to you from Sheba with certain news﴾, and informed him that she had a mighty throne. So Sulayman ﷺ said to him: ﴿We will see whether you have told the truth or whether you are among the liars﴾. His testing of the hoopoe's truthfulness from his lying was by saying to these: "Which of you will bring me the throne of this woman before they come to me in submission?" They said: Sulayman only wrote the letter with the hoopoe to the woman after his confirmation of the hoopoe's truthfulness, by the arrival of the one who had knowledge of her throne to him, as the hoopoe had described. They said: Had it not been so, it would have been impossible for him to write a letter with him to one who did not know whether she was in this world or not. They said: Another point is that if he had written a letter with the hoopoe to the woman before her throne came to him, and before his knowledge of the hoopoe's truthfulness in that, his saying to him ﴿We will see whether you have told the truth or whether you are among the liars﴾ would have had no meaning; for he would not have been aware of his second report, through delivering the letter to her or failing to deliver it to her, except as he had known of his first report when he said to him: ﴿And I have come to you from Sheba with certain news﴾. They said: And if there were not in the letter they carried a test of his truthfulness from his lying, and it would be impossible for the Prophet of God to say a statement that has no meaning, and he had said: ﴿We will see whether you have told the truth or whether you are among the liars﴾, he knew that the test by which the hoopoe's truthfulness from his lying would be distinguished was the arrival of the woman's throne to him, as the hoopoe, the witness to his truthfulness, had informed him. Then the letter was with him after that, to her.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Indeed Sulayman was given kingship, and he did not know that anyone had been given kingship other than himself. When the hoopoe was missing, he asked it: "From where have you come?" and threatened it with a severe warning of killing and punishment. It said: ﴿And I have come to you from Sheba with certain news﴾. Sulayman said to it: "What is this news?" The hoopoe said: ﴿Indeed, I found a woman﴾ in Sheba ﴿ruling over them, and she has been given of everything, and she has a mighty throne﴾. When the hoopoe informed Sulayman that it had found a sovereign, he denied that anyone on earth had sovereignty other than himself, and said to those around him of the jinn and mankind: ﴿O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾ ﴿An ifrit of the jinn said: "I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it."﴾ Sulayman said: "I want something quicker than that." ﴿The one who had knowledge of the Scripture﴾, and he was a man from mankind who had knowledge of the Scripture, in which was the greatest Name of God, by which, when called upon, He answers. ﴿I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you.﴾ So he called upon the Name while he was standing there, and the throne was carried along until it was placed before Sulayman, and God did that. When Sulayman had the throne brought, and they were polytheists who prostrated to the sun and moon, the hoopoe informed him of that, so he wrote a letter with it and sent it to them, until when the hoopoe came to the queen, it cast the letter to her ﴿She said: "O assembly, indeed a noble letter has been delivered to me..."﴾ up to ﴿and come to me in submission﴾. She said to her people what she said: ﴿And indeed I am sending a gift to them, and I will wait to see what the messengers return with﴾. He said: She sent to him boys and girls, and dressed them in one garment, so that the male could not be distinguished from the female, and she said: "If he separates them so that the male is recognized from the female, then he is a prophet, and he returns the gift; and it is fitting for us to abandon our kingship and follow his religion and join him." So Sulayman returned the gift and separated them, and said: "These are boys and these are girls." And he said: ﴿Will you aid me with wealth? What God has given me is better than what He has given you; rather, you rejoice in your gift﴾... to the end of the verse.

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, I found a woman ruling over them﴾... the verse. He said: Sulayman denied that anyone on earth had sovereignty other than himself, and said to those around him of the jinn and mankind: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne?﴾... the verse.

Others said: Rather, the hoopoe's truthfulness was tested by Sulayman through the letter, and he asked those with him to bring the woman's throne only after her messengers had left him, and after the woman herself had come toward him.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When the messengers returned to her with what Sulayman had said, she said: "By God, I know this is not a king, and we have no power against him, and we can do nothing by contending with him." And she sent: "I am coming to you with the nobles of my people, so that I may see what your command is, and what you call to of your religion." Then she ordered the throne of her kingship, on which she used to sit, which was of gold, inlaid with ruby, chrysolite and pearls, to be placed within seven chambers, one inside another, and then she locked the doors upon it. She was served only by women, with six hundred women serving her. Then she said to whomever she left in charge of her sovereignty: "Guard what is with you, and my throne; let no one of God's servants reach it, and let no one see it, until I come to you." Then she set out toward Sulayman with twelve thousand chieftains with her from the kings of Yemen, under the command of each chieftain were many thousands. Sulayman began sending the jinn, who brought him news of her march and its destination every day and night, until when she drew near, he gathered those under his command of the jinn and mankind, and said: ﴿O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾

The meaning of the speech: Sulayman said to the nobles of the jinn and mankind present with his army: ﴿O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne?﴾ meaning her couch.

As:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne?﴾ He said: a couch on a dais.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: Her throne is a couch on a dais. Ibn Jurayj said: a couch of gold, its legs of jewels and pearls.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne?﴾ — her couch.

Ibn Zayd said regarding this: Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne?﴾ He said: her seat of sitting.

The scholars differed concerning the reason why Sulayman singled out the request of the nobles of his army to bring this woman's throne from among her possessions before her conversion to Islam. Some of them said: He only did that because he was pleased with it when the hoopoe described it to him, and he feared that she would embrace Islam, whereupon her wealth would become forbidden to him, so he wished to take that throne before taking it became forbidden to him by her Islam.

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: The hoopoe informed Sulayman that she had set out to come to him, and informed him of her throne, and he was pleased with it. It was of gold, its legs of jewels, adorned with pearls, so he knew that if they came to him in submission their possessions would not be lawful to him, so he said to the jinn: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾

Others said: Rather Sulayman did that to reproach her with it, and to test her intellect: would she affirm it when she saw it, or would she deny it?

Mention of those who said this:

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: God informed Sulayman that she would come to him, so he said: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾ so that he might reproach her, and kings used to reproach one another with knowledge.

The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of His words ﴿before they come to me in submission﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is: before they come to me submitting willingly.

Mention of those who said this:

Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿before they come to me in submission﴾ — he said: obedient.

Others said: rather its meaning is: before they come to me as Muslims, in the Islam which is the religion of God.

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾ — by the sanctity of Islam, which protects them and their possessions; that is, Islam protects them.

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the opinions concerning the reason why Sulayman singled out the request of the nobles of his army to bring this woman's throne, rather than the rest of her possessions, is in our view: so that this would be a proof against her regarding his prophethood, and to make her know through it the power of God and the greatness of His affair, that she had locked it within chambers, one inside another, shut and locked upon her; and God brought it out from all that without opening locks or bolts, until He delivered it to him, and handed it over to him. This was for her the greatest proof of the truth of what Sulayman called her to, and of Sulayman's truthfulness regarding what he had informed her of his prophethood.

As for the more correct of the two interpretations of His words ﴿before they come to me in submission﴾, according to its interpretation, it is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas which we mentioned before, that its meaning is obedient, because the woman had not come to Sulayman as a Muslim; rather she embraced Islam after her arrival before him and after a dialogue and questioning that took place between them.

* *

His words: ﴿An ifrit of the jinn said﴾

His, may He be exalted, meaning: A chief of the jinn, a powerful rebellious one, said. The Arabs have two forms of it: 'ifrit and 'ifriyah; whoever says 'ifriyah makes its plural 'afari; whoever says 'ifrit makes its plural 'afarit.

The interpreters have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: ﴿An ifrit of the jinn said﴾ — a rebellious one of the jinn ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place﴾.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah and others, the like of it.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from one of his companions: ﴿An ifrit said﴾ — a calamity.

He said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Wahb ibn Sulayman informed me, from Shu'ayb al-Jaba'i, who said: The ifrit whom God mentioned: his name is Kawzan.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge: ﴿An ifrit said﴾ — his name: Kawzan.

* *

His words: ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place﴾

He says: I will bring you her throne before you rise from this seat of yours.

It was mentioned that he was sitting to judge between the people, so he said: I will bring it to you before you rise from this assembly in which you have sat to judge between people. It was mentioned that he would sit until midday.

The interpreters have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

He said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah and others, the like of it, and he said: He used to judge; he said: before you rise from your assembly in which you judge.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place﴾ — meaning his assembly.

* *

His words: ﴿And indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it﴾

Over what is in it of jewels, and I will not betray in it.

It has been said: trustworthy over the woman's private parts.

Mention of those who said this:

Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it﴾ — he said: strong to carry it, trustworthy over the private parts of this woman.

* *

His words: ﴿He said, the one who had knowledge of the Scripture﴾

His, may He be exalted, meaning: He said, the one who had knowledge of God's Scripture, and he was a man, it is mentioned, from the sons of Adam. Some of them said: his name was Balikha.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Uthmah narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Bishr, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿He said, the one who had knowledge of the Scripture﴾ — he said: his name was Balikha.

Yahya ibn Dawud al-Wasiti narrated to me, he said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, regarding His words: ﴿the one who had knowledge of the Scripture﴾ — a man from mankind.

Ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, he said: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah al-Fazari narrated to us, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Karim, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God: ﴿He said, the one who had knowledge of the Scripture: I will bring it to you﴾ — he said: I look into my Lord's Scripture, then I bring it to you ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾. He said: That scholar then spoke a word, and the throne entered beneath the earth until it emerged before them.

Ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, he said: Hammad ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from 'Uthman ibn Matar, from al-Zuhri, who said: The one who had knowledge of the Scripture called: "O our God and God of everything, one God, there is no god but You, bring me her throne." He said: So it was placed before him.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿He said, the one who had knowledge of the Scripture﴾ — he said: a man of the sons of Adam, I think he said: of the Children of Israel, who knew the Name of God by which, when called upon, He answers.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿the one who had knowledge of the Scripture﴾ — he said: the Name which, when called upon, He answers, and it is: "O Possessor of Majesty and Honour."

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say: Sulayman said to those around him: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾ The ifrit said: ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place.﴾ Sulayman said: "I want something quicker than that." So a man from mankind who had knowledge of the Scripture said — meaning the Name of God, which when called upon, He answers.

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿He said: An ifrit of the jinn: I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it﴾ — "I will not bring you anything other than it; I would say something else and give you a likeness." He said: On that day there came out a worshipful man on an island in the sea, and when he heard the ifrit say ﴿I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you﴾, he said: Then he called upon one of God's Names, and behold, it was carried between his eyes; and he recited: ﴿So when he saw it settled in his presence, he said: "This is of the bounty of my Lord"﴾ ... until ﴿indeed my Lord is Free of need and Generous.﴾

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: A man from mankind said.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verse 38–40 (part 2 of 2):

He said: Mujahid said: "The one who had knowledge of the Book" means: knowledge of the Name of Allah.

Others said: "The one who had knowledge of the Book" was Asaf.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿A ifrit (ʿifrīt) among the jinn said﴾ to Solomon, ﴿"I will bring it to you before you rise from your place. Indeed, I am strong and trustworthy for it."﴾ They claim that Solomon son of David said: "I desire something quicker than this." So Asaf ibn Barkhiya, who was a righteous man (ṣiddīq) and knew the Greatest Name (al-ism al-aʿẓam), by which when Allah is called upon He answers, and when asked by it He gives, said: ﴿"I will bring it to you"﴾ O Prophet of Allah, ﴿"before your glance returns to you."﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿"I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you."﴾

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is: "I will bring it to you before anyone from your side who is within the range of sight reaches you."

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾ — he said: "Before the farthest one you see returns to you; that is His saying ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾."

Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: someone other than Qatadah said: ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾ — "before the figure comes to you from the range of sight."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "before your glance reaches its extent and its limit."

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾ — "You stretch your eyes so that your glance does not end at its limit until I have placed it before you." He said: "That is what is meant."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Uthām narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I was informed that he said: "Raise your glance toward where it will come from," so his glance did not return to him until the throne was placed before him.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾ — he said: "The extent of his sight."

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾ — he said: "When the sight is extended until the glance returns dazzled (khāsi'an)."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾ — he said: "When the sight is extended until the glance becomes exhausted (yahsar)."

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two opinions regarding this, in terms of truth, is the view of the one who said: "before your glance returns to you from the furthest point of its trace." This is because the meaning of His saying ﴿yartadda ilayka﴾ ("returns to you") is that sight returns to you when the eye is opened, not returning, but rather extending forward until it reaches the limit of its light's extension. Since this is so, and since Allah has informed us of the speaker of this saying ﴿"I will bring it to you before it returns"﴾, it would not be for us to say: "I will bring it to you before it returns, going back ﴿to you, your glance﴾ from its endpoint."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So when he saw it settled near him﴾

He says: when Solomon saw the throne of the Queen of Sheba settled beside him. In the speech there is an omitted part, which is understood from what appears, namely: so he called upon Allah, and it was brought; then when Solomon saw it settled near him. It is mentioned that the knowledgeable one called upon Allah, so the throne sank into the ground in the place where it was, then it emerged from beneath the earth before Solomon.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: They mention that Asaf ibn Barkhiya performed ablution, then prayed two rak'ahs, then said: "O Prophet of Allah, widen your eye until your glance reaches its limit." So Solomon widened his eye, looking toward Yemen. Asaf called upon Allah, and the throne split open in its place where it was, then emerged before Solomon. ﴿So when he saw it﴾ Solomon ﴿settled near him, he said: "This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me"﴾ ... the verse.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Its throne burst forth from beneath the earth.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He said: "This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me"﴾

He says: this sight, this capacity, this dominion and authority in which I am, to the extent that her throne was brought to me within the span of the return of a glance from Ma'rib to Syria, is of the bounty of my Lord which He has bestowed upon me and His gift which He has generously given to me, in order to test me, that is, to try me and examine me: whether I will thank Him for that which He has done for me, or I will deny His favour upon me by abandoning gratitude to Him.

It has been said that its meaning is: "Shall I give thanks for the throne of this woman, since I have brought it, or shall I disbelieve, since I have seen one lower than me in the world who is more knowledgeable than me?"

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurasani informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿So when he saw it settled near him, he said: "This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me: shall I give thanks"﴾ for the throne when I was brought it ﴿"or shall I disbelieve"﴾ when I saw one lower than me in the world who is more knowledgeable than me?

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever gives thanks, he gives thanks only for his own soul﴾

He says: whoever gives thanks for Allah's blessing upon him and His favour upon him, he only gives thanks seeking benefit for his own soul, because no one other than himself benefits from that; for Allah has no need of any of His creation, and He only called them to His thanks as an exposure to benefit for them, not to acquire any benefit for Himself by their thanking Him, nor to ward off harm from Himself. ﴿And whoever disbelieves, then indeed my Lord is Self-Sufficient, Generous﴾ — He says: whoever denies His blessings and His kindness toward him and His favour upon him, has wronged his own soul and diminished its share; and Allah is free of His thanks, having no need for it, and the disbelief of those among His creation who disbelieve in Him does not harm Him. He is Generous, and among His generosity is that He bestows favour upon those who deny His blessings, and makes them a means by which they reach His disobedience.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verses 38–40 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿He said: "O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?" (38) An ifrit of the jinn said: "I will bring it to you before you rise from your place. Indeed, I am strong and trustworthy for it." (39) He said, the one who had knowledge of the Scripture: "I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you." And when he saw it settled in his presence, he said: "This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful, his gratitude is only for himself; and whoever is ungrateful, indeed my Lord is Free of need and Generous." (40)﴾

The scholars differed concerning the time at which Sulayman said: ﴿O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne?﴾ Some of them said: He said that when the hoopoe (al-hudhud) brought him the news of the Queen of Sheba, and said to him: ﴿And I have come to you from Sheba with certain news﴾, and informed him that she had a mighty throne. So Sulayman ﷺ said to him: ﴿We will see whether you have told the truth or whether you are among the liars﴾. His testing of the hoopoe's truthfulness from his lying was by saying to these: "Which of you will bring me the throne of this woman before they come to me in submission?" They said: Sulayman only wrote the letter with the hoopoe to the woman after his confirmation of the hoopoe's truthfulness, by the arrival of the one who had knowledge of her throne to him, as the hoopoe had described. They said: Had it not been so, it would have been impossible for him to write a letter with him to one who did not know whether she was in this world or not. They said: Another point is that if he had written a letter with the hoopoe to the woman before her throne came to him, and before his knowledge of the hoopoe's truthfulness in that, his saying to him ﴿We will see whether you have told the truth or whether you are among the liars﴾ would have had no meaning; for he would not have been aware of his second report, through delivering the letter to her or failing to deliver it to her, except as he had known of his first report when he said to him: ﴿And I have come to you from Sheba with certain news﴾. They said: And if there were not in the letter they carried a test of his truthfulness from his lying, and it would be impossible for the Prophet of God to say a statement that has no meaning, and he had said: ﴿We will see whether you have told the truth or whether you are among the liars﴾, he knew that the test by which the hoopoe's truthfulness from his lying would be distinguished was the arrival of the woman's throne to him, as the hoopoe, the witness to his truthfulness, had informed him. Then the letter was with him after that, to her.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Indeed Sulayman was given kingship, and he did not know that anyone had been given kingship other than himself. When the hoopoe was missing, he asked it: "From where have you come?" and threatened it with a severe warning of killing and punishment. It said: ﴿And I have come to you from Sheba with certain news﴾. Sulayman said to it: "What is this news?" The hoopoe said: ﴿Indeed, I found a woman﴾ in Sheba ﴿ruling over them, and she has been given of everything, and she has a mighty throne﴾. When the hoopoe informed Sulayman that it had found a sovereign, he denied that anyone on earth had sovereignty other than himself, and said to those around him of the jinn and mankind: ﴿O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾ ﴿An ifrit of the jinn said: "I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it."﴾ Sulayman said: "I want something quicker than that." ﴿The one who had knowledge of the Scripture﴾, and he was a man from mankind who had knowledge of the Scripture, in which was the greatest Name of God, by which, when called upon, He answers. ﴿I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you.﴾ So he called upon the Name while he was standing there, and the throne was carried along until it was placed before Sulayman, and God did that. When Sulayman had the throne brought, and they were polytheists who prostrated to the sun and moon, the hoopoe informed him of that, so he wrote a letter with it and sent it to them, until when the hoopoe came to the queen, it cast the letter to her ﴿She said: "O assembly, indeed a noble letter has been delivered to me..."﴾ up to ﴿and come to me in submission﴾. She said to her people what she said: ﴿And indeed I am sending a gift to them, and I will wait to see what the messengers return with﴾. He said: She sent to him boys and girls, and dressed them in one garment, so that the male could not be distinguished from the female, and she said: "If he separates them so that the male is recognized from the female, then he is a prophet, and he returns the gift; and it is fitting for us to abandon our kingship and follow his religion and join him." So Sulayman returned the gift and separated them, and said: "These are boys and these are girls." And he said: ﴿Will you aid me with wealth? What God has given me is better than what He has given you; rather, you rejoice in your gift﴾... to the end of the verse.

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, I found a woman ruling over them﴾... the verse. He said: Sulayman denied that anyone on earth had sovereignty other than himself, and said to those around him of the jinn and mankind: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne?﴾... the verse.

Others said: Rather, the hoopoe's truthfulness was tested by Sulayman through the letter, and he asked those with him to bring the woman's throne only after her messengers had left him, and after the woman herself had come toward him.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When the messengers returned to her with what Sulayman had said, she said: "By God, I know this is not a king, and we have no power against him, and we can do nothing by contending with him." And she sent: "I am coming to you with the nobles of my people, so that I may see what your command is, and what you call to of your religion." Then she ordered the throne of her kingship, on which she used to sit, which was of gold, inlaid with ruby, chrysolite and pearls, to be placed within seven chambers, one inside another, and then she locked the doors upon it. She was served only by women, with six hundred women serving her. Then she said to whomever she left in charge of her sovereignty: "Guard what is with you, and my throne; let no one of God's servants reach it, and let no one see it, until I come to you." Then she set out toward Sulayman with twelve thousand chieftains with her from the kings of Yemen, under the command of each chieftain were many thousands. Sulayman began sending the jinn, who brought him news of her march and its destination every day and night, until when she drew near, he gathered those under his command of the jinn and mankind, and said: ﴿O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾

The meaning of the speech: Sulayman said to the nobles of the jinn and mankind present with his army: ﴿O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne?﴾ meaning her couch.

As:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne?﴾ He said: a couch on a dais.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: Her throne is a couch on a dais. Ibn Jurayj said: a couch of gold, its legs of jewels and pearls.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne?﴾ — her couch.

Ibn Zayd said regarding this: Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne?﴾ He said: her seat of sitting.

The scholars differed concerning the reason why Sulayman singled out the request of the nobles of his army to bring this woman's throne from among her possessions before her conversion to Islam. Some of them said: He only did that because he was pleased with it when the hoopoe described it to him, and he feared that she would embrace Islam, whereupon her wealth would become forbidden to him, so he wished to take that throne before taking it became forbidden to him by her Islam.

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: The hoopoe informed Sulayman that she had set out to come to him, and informed him of her throne, and he was pleased with it. It was of gold, its legs of jewels, adorned with pearls, so he knew that if they came to him in submission their possessions would not be lawful to him, so he said to the jinn: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾

Others said: Rather Sulayman did that to reproach her with it, and to test her intellect: would she affirm it when she saw it, or would she deny it?

Mention of those who said this:

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: God informed Sulayman that she would come to him, so he said: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾ so that he might reproach her, and kings used to reproach one another with knowledge.

The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of His words ﴿before they come to me in submission﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is: before they come to me submitting willingly.

Mention of those who said this:

Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿before they come to me in submission﴾ — he said: obedient.

Others said: rather its meaning is: before they come to me as Muslims, in the Islam which is the religion of God.

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾ — by the sanctity of Islam, which protects them and their possessions; that is, Islam protects them.

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the opinions concerning the reason why Sulayman singled out the request of the nobles of his army to bring this woman's throne, rather than the rest of her possessions, is in our view: so that this would be a proof against her regarding his prophethood, and to make her know through it the power of God and the greatness of His affair, that she had locked it within chambers, one inside another, shut and locked upon her; and God brought it out from all that without opening locks or bolts, until He delivered it to him, and handed it over to him. This was for her the greatest proof of the truth of what Sulayman called her to, and of Sulayman's truthfulness regarding what he had informed her of his prophethood.

As for the more correct of the two interpretations of His words ﴿before they come to me in submission﴾, according to its interpretation, it is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas which we mentioned before, that its meaning is obedient, because the woman had not come to Sulayman as a Muslim; rather she embraced Islam after her arrival before him and after a dialogue and questioning that took place between them.

* *

His words: ﴿An ifrit of the jinn said﴾

His, may He be exalted, meaning: A chief of the jinn, a powerful rebellious one, said. The Arabs have two forms of it: 'ifrit and 'ifriyah; whoever says 'ifriyah makes its plural 'afari; whoever says 'ifrit makes its plural 'afarit.

The interpreters have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: ﴿An ifrit of the jinn said﴾ — a rebellious one of the jinn ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place﴾.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah and others, the like of it.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from one of his companions: ﴿An ifrit said﴾ — a calamity.

He said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Wahb ibn Sulayman informed me, from Shu'ayb al-Jaba'i, who said: The ifrit whom God mentioned: his name is Kawzan.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge: ﴿An ifrit said﴾ — his name: Kawzan.

* *

His words: ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place﴾

He says: I will bring you her throne before you rise from this seat of yours.

It was mentioned that he was sitting to judge between the people, so he said: I will bring it to you before you rise from this assembly in which you have sat to judge between people. It was mentioned that he would sit until midday.

The interpreters have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

He said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah and others, the like of it, and he said: He used to judge; he said: before you rise from your assembly in which you judge.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place﴾ — meaning his assembly.

* *

His words: ﴿And indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it﴾

Over what is in it of jewels, and I will not betray in it.

It has been said: trustworthy over the woman's private parts.

Mention of those who said this:

Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it﴾ — he said: strong to carry it, trustworthy over the private parts of this woman.

* *

His words: ﴿He said, the one who had knowledge of the Scripture﴾

His, may He be exalted, meaning: He said, the one who had knowledge of God's Scripture, and he was a man, it is mentioned, from the sons of Adam. Some of them said: his name was Balikha.

Mention of those who said this:
