Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Uthmah narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Bishr, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿He said, the one who had knowledge of the Scripture﴾ — he said: his name was Balikha.

Yahya ibn Dawud al-Wasiti narrated to me, he said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, regarding His words: ﴿the one who had knowledge of the Scripture﴾ — a man from mankind.

Ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, he said: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah al-Fazari narrated to us, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Karim, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God: ﴿He said, the one who had knowledge of the Scripture: I will bring it to you﴾ — he said: I look into my Lord's Scripture, then I bring it to you ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾. He said: That scholar then spoke a word, and the throne entered beneath the earth until it emerged before them.

Ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, he said: Hammad ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from 'Uthman ibn Matar, from al-Zuhri, who said: The one who had knowledge of the Scripture called: "O our God and God of everything, one God, there is no god but You, bring me her throne." He said: So it was placed before him.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿He said, the one who had knowledge of the Scripture﴾ — he said: a man of the sons of Adam, I think he said: of the Children of Israel, who knew the Name of God by which, when called upon, He answers.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿the one who had knowledge of the Scripture﴾ — he said: the Name which, when called upon, He answers, and it is: "O Possessor of Majesty and Honour."

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say: Sulayman said to those around him: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾ The ifrit said: ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place.﴾ Sulayman said: "I want something quicker than that." So a man from mankind who had knowledge of the Scripture said — meaning the Name of God, which when called upon, He answers.

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿He said: An ifrit of the jinn: I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it﴾ — "I will not bring you anything other than it; I would say something else and give you a likeness." He said: On that day there came out a worshipful man on an island in the sea, and when he heard the ifrit say ﴿I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you﴾, he said: Then he called upon one of God's Names, and behold, it was carried between his eyes; and he recited: ﴿So when he saw it settled in his presence, he said: "This is of the bounty of my Lord"﴾ ... until ﴿indeed my Lord is Free of need and Generous.﴾

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: A man from mankind said.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verse 38–40 (part 2 of 2):

He said: Mujahid said: "The one who had knowledge of the Book" means: knowledge of the Name of Allah.

Others said: "The one who had knowledge of the Book" was Asaf.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿A ifrit (ʿifrīt) among the jinn said﴾ to Solomon, ﴿"I will bring it to you before you rise from your place. Indeed, I am strong and trustworthy for it."﴾ They claim that Solomon son of David said: "I desire something quicker than this." So Asaf ibn Barkhiya, who was a righteous man (ṣiddīq) and knew the Greatest Name (al-ism al-aʿẓam), by which when Allah is called upon He answers, and when asked by it He gives, said: ﴿"I will bring it to you"﴾ O Prophet of Allah, ﴿"before your glance returns to you."﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿"I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you."﴾

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is: "I will bring it to you before anyone from your side who is within the range of sight reaches you."

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾ — he said: "Before the farthest one you see returns to you; that is His saying ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾."

Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: someone other than Qatadah said: ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾ — "before the figure comes to you from the range of sight."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "before your glance reaches its extent and its limit."

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾ — "You stretch your eyes so that your glance does not end at its limit until I have placed it before you." He said: "That is what is meant."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Uthām narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I was informed that he said: "Raise your glance toward where it will come from," so his glance did not return to him until the throne was placed before him.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾ — he said: "The extent of his sight."

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾ — he said: "When the sight is extended until the glance returns dazzled (khāsi'an)."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾ — he said: "When the sight is extended until the glance becomes exhausted (yahsar)."

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two opinions regarding this, in terms of truth, is the view of the one who said: "before your glance returns to you from the furthest point of its trace." This is because the meaning of His saying ﴿yartadda ilayka﴾ ("returns to you") is that sight returns to you when the eye is opened, not returning, but rather extending forward until it reaches the limit of its light's extension. Since this is so, and since Allah has informed us of the speaker of this saying ﴿"I will bring it to you before it returns"﴾, it would not be for us to say: "I will bring it to you before it returns, going back ﴿to you, your glance﴾ from its endpoint."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So when he saw it settled near him﴾

He says: when Solomon saw the throne of the Queen of Sheba settled beside him. In the speech there is an omitted part, which is understood from what appears, namely: so he called upon Allah, and it was brought; then when Solomon saw it settled near him. It is mentioned that the knowledgeable one called upon Allah, so the throne sank into the ground in the place where it was, then it emerged from beneath the earth before Solomon.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: They mention that Asaf ibn Barkhiya performed ablution, then prayed two rak'ahs, then said: "O Prophet of Allah, widen your eye until your glance reaches its limit." So Solomon widened his eye, looking toward Yemen. Asaf called upon Allah, and the throne split open in its place where it was, then emerged before Solomon. ﴿So when he saw it﴾ Solomon ﴿settled near him, he said: "This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me"﴾ ... the verse.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Its throne burst forth from beneath the earth.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He said: "This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me"﴾

He says: this sight, this capacity, this dominion and authority in which I am, to the extent that her throne was brought to me within the span of the return of a glance from Ma'rib to Syria, is of the bounty of my Lord which He has bestowed upon me and His gift which He has generously given to me, in order to test me, that is, to try me and examine me: whether I will thank Him for that which He has done for me, or I will deny His favour upon me by abandoning gratitude to Him.

It has been said that its meaning is: "Shall I give thanks for the throne of this woman, since I have brought it, or shall I disbelieve, since I have seen one lower than me in the world who is more knowledgeable than me?"

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurasani informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿So when he saw it settled near him, he said: "This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me: shall I give thanks"﴾ for the throne when I was brought it ﴿"or shall I disbelieve"﴾ when I saw one lower than me in the world who is more knowledgeable than me?

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever gives thanks, he gives thanks only for his own soul﴾

He says: whoever gives thanks for Allah's blessing upon him and His favour upon him, he only gives thanks seeking benefit for his own soul, because no one other than himself benefits from that; for Allah has no need of any of His creation, and He only called them to His thanks as an exposure to benefit for them, not to acquire any benefit for Himself by their thanking Him, nor to ward off harm from Himself. ﴿And whoever disbelieves, then indeed my Lord is Self-Sufficient, Generous﴾ — He says: whoever denies His blessings and His kindness toward him and His favour upon him, has wronged his own soul and diminished its share; and Allah is free of His thanks, having no need for it, and the disbelief of those among His creation who disbelieve in Him does not harm Him. He is Generous, and among His generosity is that He bestows favour upon those who deny His blessings, and makes them a means by which they reach His disobedience.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verses 38–40 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿He said: "O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?" (38) An ifrit of the jinn said: "I will bring it to you before you rise from your place. Indeed, I am strong and trustworthy for it." (39) He said, the one who had knowledge of the Scripture: "I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you." And when he saw it settled in his presence, he said: "This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful, his gratitude is only for himself; and whoever is ungrateful, indeed my Lord is Free of need and Generous." (40)﴾

The scholars differed concerning the time at which Sulayman said: ﴿O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne?﴾ Some of them said: He said that when the hoopoe (al-hudhud) brought him the news of the Queen of Sheba, and said to him: ﴿And I have come to you from Sheba with certain news﴾, and informed him that she had a mighty throne. So Sulayman ﷺ said to him: ﴿We will see whether you have told the truth or whether you are among the liars﴾. His testing of the hoopoe's truthfulness from his lying was by saying to these: "Which of you will bring me the throne of this woman before they come to me in submission?" They said: Sulayman only wrote the letter with the hoopoe to the woman after his confirmation of the hoopoe's truthfulness, by the arrival of the one who had knowledge of her throne to him, as the hoopoe had described. They said: Had it not been so, it would have been impossible for him to write a letter with him to one who did not know whether she was in this world or not. They said: Another point is that if he had written a letter with the hoopoe to the woman before her throne came to him, and before his knowledge of the hoopoe's truthfulness in that, his saying to him ﴿We will see whether you have told the truth or whether you are among the liars﴾ would have had no meaning; for he would not have been aware of his second report, through delivering the letter to her or failing to deliver it to her, except as he had known of his first report when he said to him: ﴿And I have come to you from Sheba with certain news﴾. They said: And if there were not in the letter they carried a test of his truthfulness from his lying, and it would be impossible for the Prophet of God to say a statement that has no meaning, and he had said: ﴿We will see whether you have told the truth or whether you are among the liars﴾, he knew that the test by which the hoopoe's truthfulness from his lying would be distinguished was the arrival of the woman's throne to him, as the hoopoe, the witness to his truthfulness, had informed him. Then the letter was with him after that, to her.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Indeed Sulayman was given kingship, and he did not know that anyone had been given kingship other than himself. When the hoopoe was missing, he asked it: "From where have you come?" and threatened it with a severe warning of killing and punishment. It said: ﴿And I have come to you from Sheba with certain news﴾. Sulayman said to it: "What is this news?" The hoopoe said: ﴿Indeed, I found a woman﴾ in Sheba ﴿ruling over them, and she has been given of everything, and she has a mighty throne﴾. When the hoopoe informed Sulayman that it had found a sovereign, he denied that anyone on earth had sovereignty other than himself, and said to those around him of the jinn and mankind: ﴿O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾ ﴿An ifrit of the jinn said: "I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it."﴾ Sulayman said: "I want something quicker than that." ﴿The one who had knowledge of the Scripture﴾, and he was a man from mankind who had knowledge of the Scripture, in which was the greatest Name of God, by which, when called upon, He answers. ﴿I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you.﴾ So he called upon the Name while he was standing there, and the throne was carried along until it was placed before Sulayman, and God did that. When Sulayman had the throne brought, and they were polytheists who prostrated to the sun and moon, the hoopoe informed him of that, so he wrote a letter with it and sent it to them, until when the hoopoe came to the queen, it cast the letter to her ﴿She said: "O assembly, indeed a noble letter has been delivered to me..."﴾ up to ﴿and come to me in submission﴾. She said to her people what she said: ﴿And indeed I am sending a gift to them, and I will wait to see what the messengers return with﴾. He said: She sent to him boys and girls, and dressed them in one garment, so that the male could not be distinguished from the female, and she said: "If he separates them so that the male is recognized from the female, then he is a prophet, and he returns the gift; and it is fitting for us to abandon our kingship and follow his religion and join him." So Sulayman returned the gift and separated them, and said: "These are boys and these are girls." And he said: ﴿Will you aid me with wealth? What God has given me is better than what He has given you; rather, you rejoice in your gift﴾... to the end of the verse.

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, I found a woman ruling over them﴾... the verse. He said: Sulayman denied that anyone on earth had sovereignty other than himself, and said to those around him of the jinn and mankind: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne?﴾... the verse.

Others said: Rather, the hoopoe's truthfulness was tested by Sulayman through the letter, and he asked those with him to bring the woman's throne only after her messengers had left him, and after the woman herself had come toward him.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When the messengers returned to her with what Sulayman had said, she said: "By God, I know this is not a king, and we have no power against him, and we can do nothing by contending with him." And she sent: "I am coming to you with the nobles of my people, so that I may see what your command is, and what you call to of your religion." Then she ordered the throne of her kingship, on which she used to sit, which was of gold, inlaid with ruby, chrysolite and pearls, to be placed within seven chambers, one inside another, and then she locked the doors upon it. She was served only by women, with six hundred women serving her. Then she said to whomever she left in charge of her sovereignty: "Guard what is with you, and my throne; let no one of God's servants reach it, and let no one see it, until I come to you." Then she set out toward Sulayman with twelve thousand chieftains with her from the kings of Yemen, under the command of each chieftain were many thousands. Sulayman began sending the jinn, who brought him news of her march and its destination every day and night, until when she drew near, he gathered those under his command of the jinn and mankind, and said: ﴿O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾

The meaning of the speech: Sulayman said to the nobles of the jinn and mankind present with his army: ﴿O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne?﴾ meaning her couch.

As:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne?﴾ He said: a couch on a dais.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: Her throne is a couch on a dais. Ibn Jurayj said: a couch of gold, its legs of jewels and pearls.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne?﴾ — her couch.

Ibn Zayd said regarding this: Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne?﴾ He said: her seat of sitting.

The scholars differed concerning the reason why Sulayman singled out the request of the nobles of his army to bring this woman's throne from among her possessions before her conversion to Islam. Some of them said: He only did that because he was pleased with it when the hoopoe described it to him, and he feared that she would embrace Islam, whereupon her wealth would become forbidden to him, so he wished to take that throne before taking it became forbidden to him by her Islam.

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: The hoopoe informed Sulayman that she had set out to come to him, and informed him of her throne, and he was pleased with it. It was of gold, its legs of jewels, adorned with pearls, so he knew that if they came to him in submission their possessions would not be lawful to him, so he said to the jinn: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾

Others said: Rather Sulayman did that to reproach her with it, and to test her intellect: would she affirm it when she saw it, or would she deny it?

Mention of those who said this:

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: God informed Sulayman that she would come to him, so he said: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾ so that he might reproach her, and kings used to reproach one another with knowledge.

The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of His words ﴿before they come to me in submission﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is: before they come to me submitting willingly.

Mention of those who said this:

Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿before they come to me in submission﴾ — he said: obedient.

Others said: rather its meaning is: before they come to me as Muslims, in the Islam which is the religion of God.

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾ — by the sanctity of Islam, which protects them and their possessions; that is, Islam protects them.

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the opinions concerning the reason why Sulayman singled out the request of the nobles of his army to bring this woman's throne, rather than the rest of her possessions, is in our view: so that this would be a proof against her regarding his prophethood, and to make her know through it the power of God and the greatness of His affair, that she had locked it within chambers, one inside another, shut and locked upon her; and God brought it out from all that without opening locks or bolts, until He delivered it to him, and handed it over to him. This was for her the greatest proof of the truth of what Sulayman called her to, and of Sulayman's truthfulness regarding what he had informed her of his prophethood.

As for the more correct of the two interpretations of His words ﴿before they come to me in submission﴾, according to its interpretation, it is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas which we mentioned before, that its meaning is obedient, because the woman had not come to Sulayman as a Muslim; rather she embraced Islam after her arrival before him and after a dialogue and questioning that took place between them.

* *

His words: ﴿An ifrit of the jinn said﴾

His, may He be exalted, meaning: A chief of the jinn, a powerful rebellious one, said. The Arabs have two forms of it: 'ifrit and 'ifriyah; whoever says 'ifriyah makes its plural 'afari; whoever says 'ifrit makes its plural 'afarit.

The interpreters have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: ﴿An ifrit of the jinn said﴾ — a rebellious one of the jinn ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place﴾.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah and others, the like of it.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from one of his companions: ﴿An ifrit said﴾ — a calamity.

He said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Wahb ibn Sulayman informed me, from Shu'ayb al-Jaba'i, who said: The ifrit whom God mentioned: his name is Kawzan.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge: ﴿An ifrit said﴾ — his name: Kawzan.

* *

His words: ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place﴾

He says: I will bring you her throne before you rise from this seat of yours.

It was mentioned that he was sitting to judge between the people, so he said: I will bring it to you before you rise from this assembly in which you have sat to judge between people. It was mentioned that he would sit until midday.

The interpreters have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

He said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah and others, the like of it, and he said: He used to judge; he said: before you rise from your assembly in which you judge.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place﴾ — meaning his assembly.

* *

His words: ﴿And indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it﴾

Over what is in it of jewels, and I will not betray in it.

It has been said: trustworthy over the woman's private parts.

Mention of those who said this:

Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it﴾ — he said: strong to carry it, trustworthy over the private parts of this woman.

* *

His words: ﴿He said, the one who had knowledge of the Scripture﴾

His, may He be exalted, meaning: He said, the one who had knowledge of God's Scripture, and he was a man, it is mentioned, from the sons of Adam. Some of them said: his name was Balikha.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Uthmah narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Bishr, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿He said, the one who had knowledge of the Scripture﴾ — he said: his name was Balikha.

Yahya ibn Dawud al-Wasiti narrated to me, he said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, regarding His words: ﴿the one who had knowledge of the Scripture﴾ — a man from mankind.

Ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, he said: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah al-Fazari narrated to us, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Karim, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God: ﴿He said, the one who had knowledge of the Scripture: I will bring it to you﴾ — he said: I look into my Lord's Scripture, then I bring it to you ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾. He said: That scholar then spoke a word, and the throne entered beneath the earth until it emerged before them.

Ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, he said: Hammad ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from 'Uthman ibn Matar, from al-Zuhri, who said: The one who had knowledge of the Scripture called: "O our God and God of everything, one God, there is no god but You, bring me her throne." He said: So it was placed before him.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿He said, the one who had knowledge of the Scripture﴾ — he said: a man of the sons of Adam, I think he said: of the Children of Israel, who knew the Name of God by which, when called upon, He answers.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿the one who had knowledge of the Scripture﴾ — he said: the Name which, when called upon, He answers, and it is: "O Possessor of Majesty and Honour."

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say: Sulayman said to those around him: ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?﴾ The ifrit said: ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place.﴾ Sulayman said: "I want something quicker than that." So a man from mankind who had knowledge of the Scripture said — meaning the Name of God, which when called upon, He answers.

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿He said: An ifrit of the jinn: I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed I am strong and trustworthy for it﴾ — "I will not bring you anything other than it; I would say something else and give you a likeness." He said: On that day there came out a worshipful man on an island in the sea, and when he heard the ifrit say ﴿I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you﴾, he said: Then he called upon one of God's Names, and behold, it was carried between his eyes; and he recited: ﴿So when he saw it settled in his presence, he said: "This is of the bounty of my Lord"﴾ ... until ﴿indeed my Lord is Free of need and Generous.﴾

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: A man from mankind said.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verse 38–40 (part 2 of 2):

He said: Mujahid said: "The one who had knowledge of the Book" means: knowledge of the Name of Allah.

Others said: "The one who had knowledge of the Book" was Asaf.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿A ifrit (ʿifrīt) among the jinn said﴾ to Solomon, ﴿"I will bring it to you before you rise from your place. Indeed, I am strong and trustworthy for it."﴾ They claim that Solomon son of David said: "I desire something quicker than this." So Asaf ibn Barkhiya, who was a righteous man (ṣiddīq) and knew the Greatest Name (al-ism al-aʿẓam), by which when Allah is called upon He answers, and when asked by it He gives, said: ﴿"I will bring it to you"﴾ O Prophet of Allah, ﴿"before your glance returns to you."﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿"I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you."﴾

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is: "I will bring it to you before anyone from your side who is within the range of sight reaches you."

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾ — he said: "Before the farthest one you see returns to you; that is His saying ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾."

Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: someone other than Qatadah said: ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾ — "before the figure comes to you from the range of sight."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "before your glance reaches its extent and its limit."

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾ — "You stretch your eyes so that your glance does not end at its limit until I have placed it before you." He said: "That is what is meant."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Uthām narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I was informed that he said: "Raise your glance toward where it will come from," so his glance did not return to him until the throne was placed before him.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾ — he said: "The extent of his sight."

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾ — he said: "When the sight is extended until the glance returns dazzled (khāsi'an)."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾ — he said: "When the sight is extended until the glance becomes exhausted (yahsar)."

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two opinions regarding this, in terms of truth, is the view of the one who said: "before your glance returns to you from the furthest point of its trace." This is because the meaning of His saying ﴿yartadda ilayka﴾ ("returns to you") is that sight returns to you when the eye is opened, not returning, but rather extending forward until it reaches the limit of its light's extension. Since this is so, and since Allah has informed us of the speaker of this saying ﴿"I will bring it to you before it returns"﴾, it would not be for us to say: "I will bring it to you before it returns, going back ﴿to you, your glance﴾ from its endpoint."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So when he saw it settled near him﴾

He says: when Solomon saw the throne of the Queen of Sheba settled beside him. In the speech there is an omitted part, which is understood from what appears, namely: so he called upon Allah, and it was brought; then when Solomon saw it settled near him. It is mentioned that the knowledgeable one called upon Allah, so the throne sank into the ground in the place where it was, then it emerged from beneath the earth before Solomon.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: They mention that Asaf ibn Barkhiya performed ablution, then prayed two rak'ahs, then said: "O Prophet of Allah, widen your eye until your glance reaches its limit." So Solomon widened his eye, looking toward Yemen. Asaf called upon Allah, and the throne split open in its place where it was, then emerged before Solomon. ﴿So when he saw it﴾ Solomon ﴿settled near him, he said: "This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me"﴾ ... the verse.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Its throne burst forth from beneath the earth.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He said: "This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me"﴾

He says: this sight, this capacity, this dominion and authority in which I am, to the extent that her throne was brought to me within the span of the return of a glance from Ma'rib to Syria, is of the bounty of my Lord which He has bestowed upon me and His gift which He has generously given to me, in order to test me, that is, to try me and examine me: whether I will thank Him for that which He has done for me, or I will deny His favour upon me by abandoning gratitude to Him.

It has been said that its meaning is: "Shall I give thanks for the throne of this woman, since I have brought it, or shall I disbelieve, since I have seen one lower than me in the world who is more knowledgeable than me?"

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurasani informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿So when he saw it settled near him, he said: "This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me: shall I give thanks"﴾ for the throne when I was brought it ﴿"or shall I disbelieve"﴾ when I saw one lower than me in the world who is more knowledgeable than me?

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever gives thanks, he gives thanks only for his own soul﴾

He says: whoever gives thanks for Allah's blessing upon him and His favour upon him, he only gives thanks seeking benefit for his own soul, because no one other than himself benefits from that; for Allah has no need of any of His creation, and He only called them to His thanks as an exposure to benefit for them, not to acquire any benefit for Himself by their thanking Him, nor to ward off harm from Himself. ﴿And whoever disbelieves, then indeed my Lord is Self-Sufficient, Generous﴾ — He says: whoever denies His blessings and His kindness toward him and His favour upon him, has wronged his own soul and diminished its share; and Allah is free of His thanks, having no need for it, and the disbelief of those among His creation who disbelieve in Him does not harm Him. He is Generous, and among His generosity is that He bestows favour upon those who deny His blessings, and makes them a means by which they reach His disobedience.

**The interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿He said: "Disguise her throne for her; we shall see whether she will be guided, or whether she will be among those who are not guided."﴾ (41)**

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Sulayman said, when Bilqis, the queen of Saba', had been brought the throne and had herself arrived before him, to his soldiers: "Alter her throne for this woman."

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, here used in the sense of tafsir, the explanation of the Qur'an) said things similar to what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Disguise her throne for her﴾: he said, "Alter it."

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿Disguise her throne for her﴾ when she came to him: he said, "The disguising of the throne was that something was added to it and something was taken from it."

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Disguise her throne for her﴾: he said, "Alter it."

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Disguise her throne for her﴾: "It is the seat in which she sits."

- I was told by al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿Disguise her throne for her﴾: he commanded them to add to it and to take from it.

* *

As for His words ﴿we shall see whether she will be guided﴾:

He says: we shall see whether she understands, so that she confirms that the throne is hers, ﴿or whether she will be among those who are not guided﴾, meaning: among those who do not understand, so that she does not confirm her throne.

It has also been said: Sulayman only disguised her throne for her, and commanded that a palace (sarh) be built for her, because the devils had informed him that she had no intellect and that her leg was like a donkey's hoof, so he wanted to know the truth of what had been said to him about that.

The people of ta'wil said things similar to what we have said about the interpretation of His words ﴿whether she will be guided or whether she will be among those who are not guided﴾.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿we shall see whether she will be guided or whether she will be among those who are not guided﴾: he said, "Something was added to her throne and something was taken from it, in order to look at her intellect, and she was found to be of steady intellect."

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿we shall see whether she will be guided﴾: "Will she recognise it?"

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to me, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿we shall see whether she will be guided﴾: he said, "She will recognise it."

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, regarding ﴿whether she will be guided or whether she will be among those who are not guided﴾: that is, "Will she understand, or will she be among those who do not understand?" So he did that in order to see whether she would recognise it or not recognise it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verse 42:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when she arrived, it was said, "Is your throne like this?" She said, "It is as if it were it."  And we had been given knowledge before her, and we were Muslims﴾ (42)

His saying, exalted is He, means: When the Queen of Sheba came to Solomon, he had her throne brought out for her, and he said to her: ﴿Is your throne like this?﴾ She said, comparing it to it: ﴿It is as if it were it.﴾

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some of the people of knowledge ('ahl al-'ilm), from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When she reached Solomon and spoke with him, he had her throne brought out for her, then he said: ﴿Is your throne like this?﴾ She said: ﴿It is as if it were it.﴾

- Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Abu Sufyan related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿So when she arrived, it was said, "Is your throne like this?" She said, "It is as if it were it."﴾ He said: She likened it to it, and she had left it behind her.

- Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: My father used to narrate to us this entire account, meaning the account of Solomon and this woman: ﴿So when she arrived, it was said, "Is your throne like this?" She said, "It is as if it were it."﴾ He expressed doubt.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And we had been given knowledge before her﴾

His saying, exalted is He, reporting the words of Solomon, means: Solomon said: ﴿And we had been given knowledge before her﴾, that is, this woman, through God and His power over what He wills; ﴿and we were Muslims﴾, submitting to God before her.

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿And we had been given knowledge before her﴾, he said: Solomon is saying it.

- Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verse 43:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And what she used to worship besides Allah had prevented her, for she was from a disbelieving people.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And what she used to worship besides Allah prevented this woman, the Queen of Sheba, ﴿from worshipping Allah﴾, and that was her worship of the sun instead of worshipping Allah.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And what she used to worship besides Allah had prevented her﴾, he said: Her disbelief in the decree of Allah, and her worship of the idol [[It may be that a word has dropped from the phrase, namely "sadda-ha" (prevented her), as the following narration shows.]] prevented her from being guided to the truth.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿And what she used to worship besides Allah had prevented her﴾, he said: Her disbelief in the decree of Allah prevented her from being guided to the truth. And if it were said: the meaning of that is: "And Sulayman prevented her from what she used to worship besides Allah," in the sense that he barred her and stood between her and it, that would be a good interpretation. And if it were also said: "And Allah prevented her from that by granting her success in Islam," that too would be a sound interpretation.

* *

And His words: ﴿Indeed, she was from a disbelieving people.﴾

He says: Indeed, this woman was a disbeliever from a disbelieving people. The alif in His words "innaha" (indeed she) is pronounced with a kasra, as it begins a new sentence (ibtida'). As for one who interprets His words "And what she used to worship besides Allah had prevented her" according to the interpretation we have given, then "ma" (what) in His words "ma kanat ta'bud" (what she used to worship) is in the nominative position as the subject of "sadd" (prevention), because the meaning is: her ignorance and her lack of understanding did not prevent her from worshipping Allah; rather, what prevented her from worshipping Allah was her worship of the sun and the moon, and that was part of the religion of her people and her forefathers, so she followed their footsteps in it. And for one who interprets it according to the other two readings, "ma" is in the accusative position.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: "It was said to her, 'Enter the palace.' And when she saw it, she thought it was a [expanse of] water and uncovered her shins. He said, 'Indeed, it is a palace made smooth with glass.' She said, 'My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I have submitted with Sulayman to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'" (27:44)

It is mentioned that when the Queen of Sheba came to him, Sulayman ordered the devils to build for him a palace (ṣarḥ), which was like a roof made of glass, and he had water run beneath it, in order to test her intellect and her understanding in that way, similar to what she used to do by directing to him the maidservants and servants, to distinguish between the males and the females among them, [thus] rebuking her in that manner.

⁕ Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Sulayman ordered the palace, and the devils had made it for him of glass, as if it were white like water. Then he sent water beneath it, then placed his throne upon it, and he sat upon it, and the birds, the jinn and the humans gathered around him. Then he said, "Enter the palace" (27:44), to show her a kingdom more mighty than her kingdom and a dominion greater than her dominion. "And when she saw it, she thought it was a [expanse of] water and uncovered her shins" (27:44): she had no doubt that it was water she was to wade through. It was said to her, "Enter, indeed it is a palace made smooth with glass." When she stood before Sulayman, he invited her to worship Allah and reproached her for worshipping the sun instead of Allah. She spoke in the words of the zindiqs (heretics), so Sulayman fell prostrate in reverence for what she had said, and the people prostrated with him. She was dismayed when she saw Sulayman do what he did. When Sulayman raised his head, he said, "Woe to you, what did you say?" She said, "And I had forgotten what she had said." She then said, "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I have submitted with Sulayman to Allah, Lord of the worlds" (27:44), and she submitted, and her Islam was good.

It was also said: Sulayman only ordered the building of the palace as Allah described, because the jinn feared that Sulayman would marry her, so they wanted to make him disinclined toward her. They said: her legs are the legs of a donkey, and her mother was from the jinn. So Sulayman wished to know the truth of what the jinn had informed him about that.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: The jinn said to Sulayman, to make him disinclined toward Bilqis: her legs are the legs of a donkey, and her mother was from the jinn. So Sulayman ordered the palace, and it was built, and in it were confined the creatures of the sea: fish and frogs. When she saw the palace she said, "Has the son of Dawud found no punishment with which to kill me except drowning?" "She thought it was an [expanse of] water and uncovered her shins" (27:44). He said: So she had the most beautiful shins and feet of people. He said: Sulayman then wished to keep her shins from the razor, so she made depilatory cream with that cause.

It is permissible in my view that Sulayman ordered the building of the palace for both matters that Wahb mentioned and that Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi mentioned, to test her intellect and to look at her shins and feet, to know the truth of what had been said to him about her.

Mujahid used to say, concerning the meaning of ṣarḥ, what has been reported from him:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, "al-ṣarḥ": a pool of water over which Sulayman placed glass that he had clothed it with. He said: Bilqis was hairy and hairless of leg, her shins like a donkey's hoof, and her mother was a jinn.

⁕ Aḥmad ibn al-Walid al-Ramli narrated to me, he said: Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, he said: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, from Bashir ibn Nahik, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "One of the two parents of the Queen of Sheba was a jinn."

⁕ He said: Safwan ibn Salih narrated to us, he said: al-Walid narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah, from Bashir ibn Nahik, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), without mentioning al-Nadr ibn Anas.

* *

His saying: "And when she saw it, she thought it was a [expanse of] water"

He says: When the woman saw the palace, she thought, because of its whiteness and the agitation of the creatures of the water beneath it, that it was a sea's expanse, so she uncovered her shins to wade through it to Sulayman.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "It was said to her, 'Enter the palace,' and when she saw it, she thought it was a [expanse of] water." He said: It was of glass, and the water was behind it, so she thought it was an expanse.

⁕ He said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: "she thought it was a [expanse of] water" – he said: a sea.

⁕ 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, he said: Ibn Sawwar narrated to us, he said: Rawh ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: "and uncovered her shins" – and behold, they were hairy. He said: "Is there nothing that removes this?" They said: The razor. He said: The razor has no effect. So he ordered the depilatory cream, and it was prepared.

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, he said: Hafs narrated to us, from 'Imran ibn Sulayman, from 'Ikrimah and Abu Salih, who both said: When Sulayman married Bilqis, she said to him: No iron has ever touched me. Sulayman said to the devils: Look for what removes hair. They said: depilatory cream. So she was the first to make depilatory cream.

* *

His saying: "He said, 'Indeed, it is a palace made smooth with glass'"

He, may His praise be exalted, says: Sulayman said to her: Indeed this is not a sea; it is a palace made smooth with glass. That is: it is a built, raised edifice of glass.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "mumarrad" – he said: raised high (mushayyad).

* *

His saying: "She said, 'My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I have submitted with Sulayman'"

...the verse. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The woman, the Queen of Sheba, said: My Lord, indeed I wronged myself in my worship of the sun and my prostration to what is other than You, "and I have submitted with Sulayman to Allah" – she means: I have yielded with Sulayman, submitting to Allah in monotheism, singling Him out for divinity and lordship apart from all others.

Ibn Zayd used to say concerning this what has been reported:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding: "she thought it was a [expanse of] water" – he said: "It is a palace made smooth with glass." So she recognized that she had been overcome: "She said, 'My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I have submitted with Sulayman to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verse 45–46:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And We had certainly sent to Thamud their brother Salih, [saying], "Worship Allah," but they became two parties contending.﴾ (45) ﴿He said, "O my people, why do you seek to hasten evil before good? Why do you not seek forgiveness of Allah that you might receive mercy?"﴾ (46)

Exalted is He, says: ﴿And We had certainly sent to Thamud their brother Salih﴾ to worship Allah alone, without partner, and not to make any other god along with Him. ﴿But they became two parties contending﴾ means: when Salih came to them calling them to Allah, his people among Thamud became, regarding what he called them to, two parties contending. One party confirmed Salih and believed in him, and another party denied him and disbelieved in what he brought.

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿two parties contending﴾, he said: a believer and a disbeliever. Their saying: "Salih is sent," and their saying: "Salih is not sent." And by His saying ﴿yakhtasimun﴾ he means: they differ.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿So they became two parties contending﴾, he said: a believer and a disbeliever.

* *

And His saying: ﴿He said, "O my people, why do you seek to hasten evil before good?"﴾

Exalted is He, says: Salih said to his people: O my people, for what reason do you seek the punishment of Allah before mercy?

As:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Najih, from Mujahid his saying: ﴿Why do you seek to hasten evil before good?﴾, he said: "The evil" is the punishment, "before good" is before mercy.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿He said, "O my people, why do you seek to hasten evil"﴾, he said: with the punishment before good, he said: the well-being.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Why do you not seek forgiveness of Allah that you might receive mercy?﴾

He says: Why do you not repent to Allah from your disbelief, so that your Lord would forgive you the magnitude of your sin, and pardon you from His punishment of you for the great wrong you have committed?

* *

And His saying: ﴿that you might receive mercy﴾

He says: that your Lord may have mercy upon you by your seeking His forgiveness for your disbelief.

Why do you not seek forgiveness of Allah that you might receive mercy?"﴾ (46)

As:

And His saying: ﴿that you might receive mercy﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verse 47:

The discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They said, "We have taken an omen from you and from those with you." He said, "Your omen is with Allah; rather, you are a people being tested."﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Thamud said to their messenger Salih, ﴿"We have taken an omen from you and from those with you"﴾, meaning: we consider you and those among your followers with you to be ill omens, and we have divined by the birds, [believing] that harms and calamities would befall us through you and them. Salih answered them and said to them, ﴿"Your omen is with Allah"﴾, meaning: what you have divined from the birds, regarding the harms that will befall you, is with Allah, in His knowledge. He does not know which of these will come to pass: whether you think of calamities and harms, or of what you do not hope for, such as well-being, hope and what you love.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿"Your omen is with Allah"﴾, he said: "Your calamities."

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿"Your omen is with Allah"﴾, he said: "Your fate is with Allah."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿"Rather, you are a people being tested"﴾

It means: rather, you are a people being tested. Your Lord tests you since He sent me to you: will you obey Him, acting on what He has commanded you, so that He rewards you with His abundant reward? Or will you disobey Him by opposing Him, so that His punishment descends upon you?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verse 48–49:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And there were in the city nine men who caused corruption in the land and did not reform﴾ [48] ﴿They said, "Swear to one another by Allah that we will surely attack him and his family by night; then we will say to his heir, 'We did not witness the destruction of his family, and indeed we are truthful.'"﴾ [49]

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And there were in the city of Salih, which is the rocky tract of Thamud, nine persons who caused corruption in the land and did not reform." Their corruption in the land was their disbelief in Allah and their disobedience to Him. Allah, may His praise be exalted, specified these nine men in the report that they used to cause corruption in the land and did not reform, although all the people of disbelief in the land were corrupters, because these nine are the ones who, as has reached us, strove to hamstring the she-camel and cooperated in it, and swore an oath together to kill Salih from among the people of Thamud. We have mentioned their stories and reports earlier in this our book.

It is in accordance with what we have said regarding this that the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿nine men﴾, he said: "From the people of Salih."

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And there were in the city nine men who caused corruption in the land and did not reform﴾, he said: "They are the ones who hamstrung the she-camel, and when they hamstrung her they said: 'We will attack Salih and his family and kill them, then we will say to the heirs of Salih: We did not witness anything of this, and we have no knowledge of it.' So Allah destroyed them all."

* *

And His saying: ﴿They said, "Swear to one another by Allah"﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: These nine men who cause corruption in the land of the rocky tract of Thamud and do not reform said: "Swear to one another by Allah, O people, let some of you swear to others: we will surely attack Salih and his family, and we will kill him; then we will say to his heir: We did not witness the destruction of his family."

It is in accordance with what we have said regarding this that the people of interpretation have spoken.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿swear to one another by Allah﴾, he said: "They swore an oath together to destroy him, but they did not reach him, until they were destroyed along with all their people."

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, similarly.

The phrase ﴿swear to one another by Allah﴾ may be construed in two ways. One is the accusative (naṣb) as a report, as if it were said: "They said, [being] those who swear to one another." It has been mentioned that this is in the reading of 'Abd Allah: "and they do not reform, swear to one another by Allah," without "they said," and so his reading indicates the accusative in "swear" as I have described. The other way is the jussive (jazm), as if some of them said to others: "Swear by Allah." According to this second way, the reading ﴿we will surely attack﴾ with the yā' and the nūn is acceptable, because the one who said to them "swear" is among those who swear, just as it is said in speech: "Rise up with us, and we will go to so-and-so," and "Rise up, we will go to him." According to the first way, which is the accusative, the reading with the nūn is more eloquent, because its meaning is: "They said, swearing to one another, 'We will surely attack him.'" The yā' may be permitted in this way, as one says in speech: "They said, 'We will surely honour your father,'" and "He will surely honour your father." With the nūn this was read by the reciters of Medina, and the majority of the reciters of Basra and some of the Kufans. As for the more common reading among the reciters of Kufa, it is with the yā' and with the damma on the tā' together. As for some of the Meccans, he read it with the yā'.

The most preferable of the readings to me is the nūn, because that is the more eloquent speech according to the two ways I have explained, the accusative and the jussive, although all of them are sound and not corrupt for what I have described; and the one I dislike most is the reading with the yā', because of the scarcity of its readers in this form.

* *

And His saying: ﴿we will surely attack him﴾

He said: they will surely attack Salih by night and then seize him.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, he said: The nine who hamstrung the she-camel said: "Come, let us kill Salih. If he is truthful—meaning in what he promised them of punishment after the three days—we will hasten it before him; and if he is lying, we will have joined him to his she-camel." So they came to him at night to attack him in his family, but the angels struck them with stones; and when they were slow to return to their companions, they came to the dwelling of Salih and found them crushed, smashed with stones.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and indeed we are truthful﴾

They say to his heir: "And indeed we are truthful: we did not witness the destruction of his family."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verses 50–51:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they schemed a scheme, and We schemed a scheme, while they perceived not.﴾ ﴿So see how was the end of their scheme: that We destroyed them and their people, all of them.﴾

Exalted is He, says: The treachery of these nine men, the band who were corrupting in the land, against Salih, by going to him at night to kill him and his family, while Salih was unaware of this. ﴿And We schemed a scheme﴾ means: We seized them through Our punishment of them and Our hastening of the torment upon them. ﴿While they perceived not﴾ our scheme.

We have already explained earlier the meaning of "the scheme of God" against those against whom He schemes, what that signifies, and that it is His seizing those who seize them unawares, or His gradual leading on of those who disbelieve in Him and disobey Him, then His bringing down of punishment upon them when they are heedless and unaware.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shamir ibn Atiyyah, from a man, from Ali, who said: "The scheme is treachery, and treachery is disbelief."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿And they schemed a scheme, and We schemed a scheme﴾: "They plotted their affair, and God plotted for them. They schemed against Salih with a scheme, and We schemed against them with a scheme, ﴿while they perceived not﴾ Our scheme, and We perceived their scheme." They said: "Salih claims that he will finish with us within three days, so we will finish with him and his family before that." He had a mosque in al-Hijr, in a ravine, where he would pray. So they went out to a cave and said: "When he comes to pray, we will kill him, then we will return, once we have finished with him, to his family." We finished with them. He recited the saying of God, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿They said: "Swear to one another by God that we will surely attack him and his family by night, then we will surely say to his heir: 'We did not witness the destruction of his family, and indeed we are truthful.'"﴾ So God sent a rock from the mountain opposite them, and they feared it would crush them, so they hastened into the cave, and the rock sealed the mouth of that cave over them. Their people do not know where they are, nor do they know what was done to their people. So God, blessed and exalted, punished these here and those there, and God saved Salih and those with him.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And they schemed a scheme, and We schemed a scheme﴾ He said: "God empowered a rock over them, and it killed them."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿So see how was the end of their scheme﴾

Exalted is He, says: So look, O Muhammad, with the eye of your heart, at the end of the treachery of Thamud against their prophet Salih: how was it? What brought upon them their transgression, their insolence, and their denial? For that is Our way with whoever denies Our messengers and rebels against Us among the rest of creation. So warn your people, the Quraysh, that what befell Thamud for denying Salih of punishments should not befall them for denying you.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿That We destroyed them and their people, all of them﴾

He says: We destroyed the nine men, the band who were corrupting in the land, from the people of Salih, and their people from Thamud, all of them, leaving none of them.

The readers differed concerning the reading of His saying "innā" (that). The majority of the readers of Hijaz and Basra read it with a kasra (*innā*), as a new sentence. The majority of the readers of Kufa read ﴿annā dammarnāhum﴾ with a fatha on the alif. When it is read with a fatha, "annā" has two grammatical possibilities: one is the nominative, taking it as a reference back to "the end" (al-'aqibah), following it; the other is the accusative, taking it as a reference to the position of "how" (kayfa), since it is in the accusative position if you wish; or, if you wish, as a repetition of "kāna" upon it in one way: "So look how the end of their scheme was: that Our destruction of them was the end of their scheme."

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this, in my opinion, is to say: these are two well-known readings among the readers of the regions, close in meaning, and whichever of them the reader recites, he is correct.

And His saying: ﴿Rather, you are a people who are ignorant﴾

He says: "Your doing this is nothing but that you are a people who are foolish and ignorant of the great right of Allah over you, so you have opposed His command and disobeyed His Messenger."

The commentary on the words of God Most High: ﴿So the answer of his people was not but that they said, "Expel the family of Lot from your town. Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure."﴾ (27:56)

God Most High says: Then there was no answer from the people of Lot to him, when he forbade them from what God had commanded him to forbid them, namely having intercourse with men, except that some of them said to others: ﴿Expel the family of Lot from your town. Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾ from what we do, namely having intercourse with males in their anuses.

As related:

- Al-Hasan told us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: I heard al-Hasan ibn 'Umara mention, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿people who keep themselves pure﴾, he said: "From having intercourse with men and with women in their anuses."

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, he said: Abu 'Asim told us, he said: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa' told us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾, he said: "From the anuses of men and the anuses of women, mockingly at them."

- Al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, he said: ﴿keep themselves pure﴾ from the anuses of men and women, mocking them; they would say that.

- Al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, that he recited ﴿Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾ and said: "They found fault with them without any fault," meaning: they keep themselves pure from evil deeds.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿So We saved him and his family, except his wife; We decreed her to be among those who remained behind﴾ [and] ﴿We rained upon them a rain, and evil was the rain of those who were warned﴾ (57–58).

His Exalted remembrance says: So We saved Lot and his family, apart from his wife, from Our punishment when We brought it down upon them. Then ﴿qaddarnāhā﴾ means: We decreed her, meaning We made her, by Our decree, ﴿among those who remained behind﴾, among those left behind. ﴿And We rained upon them a rain﴾, which is God's raining upon them from the sky stones of baked clay (sijjil). ﴿Evil was the rain of those who were warned﴾ means: evil was that rain as the rain of the people whom God had warned of His punishment for their disobedience toward Him, and whom He had frightened with His might by sending the Messenger to them with that.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: Praise be to God, and peace be upon His servants whom He has chosen. Is God better, or what they associate?﴾ (59)

His Exalted remembrance says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿Praise be to God﴾ for His blessings upon us and His granting us success in the guidance He has granted us. ﴿And peace﴾ means: and security from Him from His punishment with which He punished the people of Lot and the people of Salih. ﴿Upon those whom He has chosen﴾ means: those whom He selected for His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), making them his companions and his ministers in the religion with which he was sent, calling to it, rather than the polytheists who associate others with Him and deny the prophethood of His Prophet.

Concerning the interpretation of this, the people of interpretation said the same as what we have said.

Mention of those who said so:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Talq, meaning Ibn Ghannam, narrated to us, from Ibn Zuhayr, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And peace upon His servants whom He has chosen﴾ – he said: "The companions of Muhammad, whom God chose for His Prophet."

Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: I said to Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak: "Tell me about God's words ﴿Say: Praise be to God, and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen﴾: who are these?" He told me from Sufyan al-Thawri, who said: "They are the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)."

* *

As for His words: ﴿Is God better, or what they associate?﴾

His Exalted remembrance says: Say, O Muhammad, to these people whose deeds We have made attractive to them among your people, so that they wander blindly: Is God, who bestowed these blessings upon His friends, which He has recounted to you in this surah, and who destroyed His enemies with the kinds of punishment He has mentioned to you therein, better; or what you associate with Him of your idols, which neither benefit you nor harm you, nor ward off evil from themselves or from their worshippers, nor bring benefit to themselves or to them? This means: this matter is not unclear to anyone who has intellect. How, then, do you deem it permissible to associate in worship with Him what has no benefit for you and no power to avert harm from you, with Him in whose hand is benefit and harm, and who possesses all things? Then Exalted is He began enumerating His blessings upon them and His favours toward them, and informing them of how little they thank Him for what He has given them, saying: ﴿Or who created the heavens and the earth?﴾
