On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: "Is He not better who created the heavens and the earth and sent down for you water from the sky, and We caused to grow thereby gardens of joyful beauty? It was not [possible] for you to make grow their trees. Is there a god with Allah? No! But they are a people who ascribe equals [to Him]." (27:60)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the polytheists among the Quraysh: Is worship of what you worship of your idols, which neither harm nor benefit, better, or worship of the One who created the heavens and the earth? "And sent down for you water from the sky," meaning rain, though it is also permissible that He intends by it the springs which He caused to gush forth in the earth, since all of that is from His creation. "And We caused to grow thereby," meaning by the water sent down from the sky, "gardens" (ḥadāʾiq), which is the plural of ḥadīqah (garden). A ḥadīqah is an orchard enclosed by a surrounding wall; if it has no wall, it is not a ḥadīqah.

* *

As for His words, "of joyful beauty":

He says: possessing a fine appearance. It has also been said that dhāt (possessing) is in the singular, and it has been said that the word is in the plural (ḥadāʾiq), as in His words: "And to Allah belong the most beautiful names" (7:180), and I have explained that previously.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, both of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words, "gardens of joyful beauty," he said: "Bahjah" is the blossoming of what people and livestock eat.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words, "gardens of joyful beauty," he said: from everything that people and livestock eat.

* *

As for His words, "It was not [possible] for you to make grow their trees":

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We caused these gardens to grow for you by the water which We sent down from the sky, for you had no capacity, had He not sent down water upon you from the sky, to make the trees of these gardens grow, and you were not able to bring about that [growth], since it is not sound except by water.

* *

As for His words, "Is there a god with Allah?":

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Is there an object of worship besides Allah, O ignorant ones, who created that, sent down water from the sky, and caused gardens to grow for you by it? His words, "Is there a god...," are construed as an interrogation meaning: "Is there a god with Allah?"

"No! But they are a people who ascribe equals [to Him]," meaning, may His praise be exalted: Rather, these polytheists are a people of error who deviate from the truth and act unjustly toward it, deliberately and knowingly, while they know that they are in error and misguidance. They do not deviate out of ignorance, as if they believed that one who cannot benefit or harm is better than the One who created the heavens and the earth and performed these acts; rather, they deviate with knowledge and certainty, following the custom of those among their fathers who came before them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verse 61:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Is He Who made the earth a stable resting place, and placed within it rivers, and placed upon it firmly set mountains, and made between the two seas a barrier? Is there a god along with Allah? Rather, most of them do not know.﴾ (61)

His, the Exalted's, saying: Is the worship of what you associate with your Lord, O people, better, when it neither harms nor benefits? Or is the One Who made the earth a resting place for you, on which you settle, so that it does not shake with you, ﴿and placed within it﴾ for you ﴿rivers﴾, meaning: placed rivers between them; ﴿and placed upon it firmly set mountains﴾, which are the immovable mountains;

﴿and made between the two seas a barrier﴾, between the sweet and the salt, so that one does not corrupt the other; ﴿Is there a god along with Allah?﴾, other than Him, who did these things, so that you associate him with your worship of Him?

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Rather, most of them do not know﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: Rather, most of these polytheists do not know the extent of Allah's greatness, nor the harm they incur by associating in the worship of Allah something other than Him, nor the benefit they gain by singling out Allah with divinity, sincerely devoting worship to Him, and disavowing every deity other than Him.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Is He who answers the distressed one when he calls upon Him, and removes the evil, and makes you successors on the earth? Is there a god along with Allah? Little do you remember.﴾ (62)

His, the Exalted's, saying means: Is what you associate with Allah better, or is the One who answers the distressed when he calls on Him, and removes from him the evil that has befallen him?

As related: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: ﴿and removes the evil﴾, he said: the harm.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and makes you successors of the earth﴾

It means: He causes living successors to succeed your rulers on the earth from among you, who will replace them.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Is there a god along with Allah?﴾

It means: Is there a god besides Allah who does these things to you and bestows these blessings upon you? As for His saying: ﴿Little do you remember﴾, it means: you remember little of Allah's greatness and His favours upon you, and you take heed of Allah's proofs against you only slightly, and therefore you have associated others with Him in worship.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verses 62–63:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Is He who guides you in the darknesses of the land and the sea, and who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy? Is there a god with Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.﴾

Says God, may He be remembered: Is what you associate with Allah better, or is He who guides you in the darknesses of the land and the sea when you lose your way in them, so that the paths become dark to you in them?

As related: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: ﴿Is He who guides you in the darknesses of the land and the sea﴾: The darkness on land is the loss of the way, and at sea, it is the loss of its course, its waves, and what happens in it.

* *

His saying: ﴿And who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy﴾

He says: And He who sends the winds as glad tidings (nushran) for the revival of dead lands before His mercy, meaning: ahead of the rain that gives life to the dead land.

* *

His saying: ﴿Is there a god with Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him﴾

Says God, may He be remembered: Is there a god with Allah, other than Allah, who does any of these things for you so that you worship him instead of Him, or associate him with Him in your worship? ﴿Exalted is Allah﴾ means: To Allah belongs the supremacy and elevation above your associating, and your worship of what you worship alongside Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verse 64–66:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is He not better who originates creation and then repeats it, and who provides for you from the sky and the earth? Is there a god with Allah? Say, "Bring your proof, if you should be truthful."﴾ (64)

His saying, exalted is He, means: Is what you associate (with Allah), O people, better, or is He who originates creation and then repeats it, bringing it into being without a precedent, then causing it to perish when He wills, then restoring it when He wills to its form before He caused it to perish; and He who provides for you from the sky and the earth, sending down rain from the sky and causing plants to grow from the earth for your sustenance and the sustenance of your livestock? ﴿Is there a god with Allah?⦆ Other than Allah, does anyone do that? If they claim that there is a god other than Allah who does that, or any part of it, then ﴿Say﴾ to them, O Muhammad, ﴿"Bring your proof"﴾, that is, your argument that something other than Allah does that, ﴿"if you should be truthful"﴾ in your claim.

As for "man" (in "Amman") and "ma" (in "Am ma yushrikun") being the subject (mubtada') in His saying, "Am ma yushrikun," and the verses after it up to His saying, ﴿and who provides for you from the sky and the earth﴾, they carry the meaning of "alladhi" (who), not the meaning of interrogation, because an interrogative does not enter upon another interrogative.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "None in the heavens and earth knows the unseen except Allah. And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected."﴾ (65) ﴿Rather, their knowledge has failed concerning the Hereafter. Rather, they are in doubt about it. Rather, they are blind to it.﴾ (66)

His saying, exalted is He, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to your questioners among the polytheists about the Hour, when it will occur: ﴿None in the heavens and earth knows the unseen﴾, which Allah has reserved for His own knowledge and withheld from His creation, and the Hour is part of that ﴿and they do not perceive﴾, meaning: those in the heavens and earth among His creation do not know when they will be raised from their graves for the establishment of the Hour.

⁕ Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, he said: Dawud ibn Abi Hind informed us, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, who said: 'A'isha said: Whoever claims that he informs people of what will happen tomorrow has greatly slandered Allah, and Allah says: ﴿None in the heavens and earth knows the unseen﴾.

The grammarians differed regarding the i'rab (grammatical case) of "illa" (except). Some of the Basran grammarians said: it is as you say: "except a few of them" (illa qalilun minhum). In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "qaliIan" (in the accusative) as a substitute for the first, because you negated it of him and made it for the other.

Some of the Kufan grammarians said: if you wish, you may assume in "man" an indefinite sense, so that it is coordinated with: "Say, no one knows the unseen except Allah." He said: It is also permissible for "man" to be definite, and what follows "illa" is placed upon it, so it is a conjunction (atf) and not a substitution (badal), because the first is negated and the second affirmed; so it is in the structure as when you say: "Zayd stood, except 'Amr," and the second is a conjunction to the first, and the sense is a denial; it is not permissible for the statement to be a denial and the denial to be a statement. He said: Likewise, ﴿They did not do it, except a few﴾ (illa qalilun). As for "qalilan" in the accusative, it is by way of exception in your worship of Him; and for the nominative, it is by way of conjunction, and not substitution.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Rather, their knowledge has failed concerning the Hereafter⦆

The readers differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Madinah, apart from Abu Ja'far, and the majority of the readers of Kufa, recited it as: ﴿Bal iddaraka﴾ with a kasra on the lam of "bal" and shaddah on the dal of "idraak", meaning: "Bal tadaraka 'ilmuhum", that is, their knowledge followed one another concerning the Hereafter, whether it would occur or not; then the ta' was assimilated into the dal, as it is said: ﴿ithaqaltum ila al-ard﴾ (9:38), which we have explained previously sufficiently.

The majority of the readers of Makkah recited: "Bal adraka 'ilmuhum fi al-akhirah", with a sukun on the dal and a fatha on the alif, meaning: "Has their knowledge attained knowledge of the Hereafter?" It is reported that Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' would reject the reading of one who recites "bal adraka", saying: "bal" is affirmative, and interrogation in this position is denial. The meaning of the speech, if recited thus, "bal adraka," would be that their knowledge did not attain the Hereafter; and Ibn Muhaysin recited it with interrogation, in the manner that Abu 'Amr had rejected.

Similar to what you have mentioned of the Makkans in their recitation, it is reported that Mujahid recited it, except that in place of "bal" he would recite "am".

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, he said: 'Uthman ibn al-Aswad narrated to us, from Mujahid, that he recited: "Am adraka 'ilmuhum".

It is reported that Ibn 'Abbas used to recite with the affirmation of a ya' in "bala", then begin "adarak" with a fatha on its alif in the form of interrogation with shaddah on the dal.

⁕ Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, he said: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this verse: "Bala adraka 'ilmuhum fi al-akhirah": that is, it did not attain.

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas recite "Bala adarak 'ilmuhum fi al-akhirah", and it is an interrogation: it did not attain.

It seems Ibn 'Abbas directed this towards the sense that it is in the manner of mockery towards those who deny the resurrection.

The correct readings in our view are the two readings you mentioned, one of which is from the readers of Makkah and Basra, namely "Bal adraka 'ilmuhum" with a sukun on the lam of "bal", fatha on the alif of "adraka", and lightening of its dal; and the other of the two from the readers of Kufa, namely ﴿Bal iddaraka﴾ with a kasra on the lam and shaddah on the dal of "idraak", because they are the two well-known readings among the readers of the metropolitan cities; so whichever of the two a reader recites, he is correct in our view. As for the reading reported from Ibn 'Abbas, although its meaning and grammar are sound, it contradicts what the codices of the Muslims contain, since in "bala" in his recitation there is an added ya' which is not in the codices, and moreover it is a reading we do not know anyone of the metropolitan readers to have recited. As for the reading reported from Ibn Muhaysin, what Abu 'Amr said about it is a sound statement, because the Arabs confirm by "bal" what follows it and do not negate it, and interrogation in this position is denial, not affirmation, since Allah has informed us that the polytheists are in doubt about the Hour, saying: ﴿Rather, they are in doubt about it. Rather, they are blind to it.﴾

The correct readings in our view are the two readings you mentioned, one of which is from the readers of Makkah and Basra, namely "Bal adraka 'ilmuhum" with a sukun on the lam of "bal", fatha on the alif of "adraka", and lightening of its dal; and the other of the two from the readers of Kufa, namely ﴿Bal iddaraka﴾ with a kasra on the lam and shaddah on the dal of "idraak", because they are the two well-known readings among the readers of the metropolitan cities; so whichever of the two a reader recites, he is correct in our view. As for the reading reported from Ibn 'Abbas, although its meaning and grammar are sound, it contradicts what the codices of the Muslims contain, since in "bala" in his recitation there is an added ya' which is not in the codices, and moreover it is a reading we do not know anyone of the metropolitan readers to have recited. As for the reading reported from Ibn Muhaysin, what Abu 'Amr said about it is a sound statement, because the Arabs confirm by "bal" what follows it and do not negate it, and interrogation in this position is denial, not affirmation, since Allah has informed us that the polytheists are in doubt about the Hour, saying: ﴿Rather, they are in doubt about it. Rather, they are blind to it.﴾

The interpreters differed in the interpretation of this. Some of them said: its meaning is: "Bal adraka 'ilmuhum fi al-akhirah", so they became certain of it when they witnessed it, when their certainty about it did not benefit them, since they had denied it in the world.

Those who said this:

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ata' al-Khurasani said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Bal adraka 'ilmuhum": he said: their sight in the Hereafter, when knowledge and sight did not benefit them.

Others said: rather, its meaning is: rather, their knowledge disappeared in the Hereafter.

Those who said this:

⁕ 'Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his saying: "Bal adraka 'ilmuhum fi al-akhirah", he says: their knowledge disappeared.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿Rather, their knowledge has failed concerning the Hereafter﴾, he said: he says: their knowledge went astray concerning the Hereafter, so they have no knowledge of it; ﴿they are blind to it﴾.

Others said: the meaning of that is: their knowledge did not reach them concerning it.

Those who said this:

⁕ 'Abd al-Warith ibn 'Abd al-Samad narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from my grandfather, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿Bal iddaraka 'ilmuhum fi al-akhirah﴾, he said: he used to recite it: "Bal adraka 'ilmuhum fi al-akhirah", he said: their knowledge did not reach them concerning it, nor do they have any desire to reach it.

Others said: the meaning of that is: "Bal adraka" means "Am adraka" (or has it attained).

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Bal adraka 'ilmuhum", he said: "Am adraka".

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Uthman narrated to us, from Mujahid: "Bal adraka 'ilmuhum", he said: "Am adraka 'ilmuhum", from where would their knowledge attain?

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings in the interpretation of this, according to the reading of one who recites "Bal adraka", is the saying we mentioned from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas, namely that its meaning is: when it is recited thus, ﴿and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected⦆ — rather, their knowledge attained that very moment in the Hereafter when they are resurrected, so their knowledge of it will not benefit them then; but in the world they were in doubt about it, rather they were blind to it.

I only said that this saying is the most correct interpretation, according to the reading mentioned, because it is the clearest of its meanings. Since that is its meaning, there is an ellipsis in the speech that is dispensed with by the indication of what appears of it, for the meaning of the speech is: "And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected; rather, they perceive that in the Hereafter. So if the speech has this meaning: 'And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected; rather their knowledge of that attained in the Hereafter; rather, in the world they are in doubt about it.'" As for the reading of one who recites ﴿Bal iddaraka﴾ with a kasra on the lam and shaddah on the dal, the saying we mentioned from Mujahid is that "bal" means "am", and the Arabs place "am" in the position of "bal" and "bal" in the position of "am" when there is an interrogative at the beginning of the speech, as the poet said:

"By Allah, I do not know whether Salma has appeared to me (taghawwalat), or is it sleep, or is it both beloved to me..."

[Footnote in the source: taghawwalat: appeared to me in dreams in various forms. The witness in the verse: the first "am" is conjunctive, since it is equivalent to the hamzah; he says: I do not know whether it is the phantom of Salma that appeared and presented itself to me, or it is sleep confusing the forms of things, which are confused dreams. As for the second "am", it is for disjunction, in the sense of "bal": he says: rather, all of that is beloved to my soul, meaning what appears to him of the phantom of imagination and what he sees in sleep of dreams. The verse is among the witnesses of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an. And in Lisan al-'Arab, under "d-r-k". As for one who recites "bal adarak", al-Farra' said: its meaning in language is "tadaraka", i.e., their knowledge followed in succession concerning the Hereafter; he means by knowledge of the Hereafter: whether it would be or not. That is why He said: "Rather, they are in doubt about it. Rather, they are blind to it." He said: In Ubayy's reading it is "am tadaraka". The Arabs place "bal" in the position of "am" and "am" in the position of "bal" when there is an interrogative at the beginning of the speech, like the poet's saying: "By Allah, I do not know..." the verse. The meaning of "am" is "bal". Abu Mu'adh al-Nahwi said: whoever recites "bal adraka" and whoever recites "bal adarak", their meaning is one. He says: they are scholars in the Hereafter, like Allah's saying: "How well they will hear and see on the day they come to Us" and the like. Al-Suddi said in his tafsir: their knowledge gathered in the Hereafter, and its meaning for him is: they came to know in the Hereafter that what they were promised was true. Al-Azhari said: the statement on the explanation of adraka and adarak and the meaning of the verse is what al-Suddi said, and what Abu Mu'adh and Abu Sa'id went to. As for what al-Farra' said about the meaning of tadaraka, i.e., their knowledge followed in succession in the Hereafter, whether it would be or not, it is not clear; rather the meaning is that their knowledge followed in succession in the Hereafter, and was settled when the Resurrection came true, and they lost, and the truth of what they were promised became manifest to them, when that knowledge will not benefit them.]]

That is, by it he means: "Rather, every one of them is beloved (to me)." So the interpretation of the speech becomes: "And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected; rather their knowledge followed in succession in the Hereafter" — that is, their knowledge of the Hereafter followed in succession; that is, it did not follow in succession in this matter, and they did not know it; rather their knowledge disappeared from it, and went astray, and they did not reach it and did not attain it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Rather, they are in doubt about it⦆

He says: Rather, these polytheists who ask you about the Hour are in doubt about its establishment; they do not hold certainty about it, nor do they believe that they will be resurrected after death. ﴿Rather, they are blind to it⦆: he says: rather, they are blind regarding knowledge of its establishment.

The commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieved said, "When we have become dust, and our fathers [as well], will we really be brought forth?" "We have certainly been promised this, we and our fathers before [us]. This is not but the fables of the former peoples."﴾ (27:67–68)

Allah, the Exalted, says: The ones who disbelieved in Allah said: "Will we really be brought out of our graves alive, in our present form after our death, after we were dust in them and had decayed?" ﴿We have certainly been promised this, we and our fathers before [us]﴾ means: this was promised to us before Muhammad by those who made promises, and they promised it to our fathers, but we have not seen any reality of it, nor have we confirmed its truth. ﴿This is not but the fables of the former peoples﴾ means: they said, "This promise is nothing but the falsehoods that the former peoples inscribed, recording them in their books, and they transmitted them without there being any truth to them."

**The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 27, verses 69–72**

**On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Say: Travel through the land and observe how was the end of the criminals﴾ (69) ﴿And do not grieve over them, and do not be in distress because of what they plot﴾ (70)**

God, dhikruhu, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to these deniers, concerning what I have brought you of the news from your Lord: ﴿Travel through the land and observe﴾ the abodes of those before you among the deniers of God's messengers, and their dwellings, how they are. Did God not ruin them and destroy their people for their denial of their messengers and their rejection of their sincere advice, so that the abodes were emptied of them and their traces and remains were effaced? That was the end of their criminality, and it is the custom of your Lord with everyone who follows their path in denying the messengers of their Lord. God will do the same to you if you do not hasten to repent of your disbelief and your denial of the messenger of your Lord.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And do not grieve over them﴾

God, dhikruhu, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Do not grieve over the turning away of these polytheists from you and their denial of you. ﴿And do not be in distress because of what they plot﴾, meaning: let your breast not be constricted by their scheming against you, for God is your helper against them, and will destroy them by the sword.

* *

**On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And they say, "When will this promise be, if you are truthful?" (71) Say, "Perhaps some of what you are hastening for has drawn near to you."﴾ (72)**

God, dhikruhu, says: The polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, who deny you concerning what you brought them from your Lord, say: ﴿When﴾ will ﴿this promise﴾ come, the promise you have made us of punishment, which, as you say, is upon us? ﴿If you are truthful﴾ in what you threaten us with. ﴿Say: "Perhaps﴾ it has drawn near to you" ﴿some of what you are hastening for﴾ of God's punishment. God, great is His majesty, says: Say to them, O Muhammad: perhaps it has come close to you and drawn near, ﴿some of what you are hastening for﴾ of God's punishment.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, i.e. exegesis) have said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ali related to me, saying: Abd Allah related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿Say: "Perhaps it has drawn near to you"﴾, that he said: it has come close to you.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿Say: "Perhaps some of what you are hastening for has drawn near to you"﴾, that he said: it has come close to you, some of what you are hastening for.

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿Perhaps it has drawn near to you﴾, he said: radifa: it has hastened upon you.

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿Say: "Perhaps some of what you are hastening for has drawn near to you"﴾, he said: it has come near.

- I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: ﴿has drawn near to you﴾: it has come close to you.

The grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyya) differed regarding the reason the lam enters in His words: ﴿radifa lakum﴾. The well-known usage of the Arabs is: radifahu amr, and aradafahu (something followed him), as one says: tabi'ahu and atba'ahu (he followed him). Some grammarians of Basra said: the lam is introduced here, thereby attaching the verb, as one says: ﴿for the dream you interpret﴾ and ﴿for their Lord they fear﴾.

Some grammarians of Kufa said: the lam is introduced here for the sake of meaning, because its meaning is: it drew near to them, as the poet said:

*"I said to her: the needs cast the youth about,*
*and they have wearied me, the mounts of their riding."*

[This is a half-line from the evidence cited by al-Farra' in (Ma'ani al-Qur'an, p. 236 of the Cairo University photographic edition), and its second half is: "and they have wearied me, the mounts of their riding." It is in (al-Lisan: ʿnā), and in its transmission the word is "ta'anahu" in place of "ta'annani". He said: 'ana al-shay' means he suffered it; one says 'anahu and ta'annahu, and ta'anna he. He said: "faqultu.." etc. The verse is evidence that the ba' in "bi-al-fata" is superfluous, like its use in His words (radifa lakum).]

So he introduced the ba' in "yatrahna" (they cast), although one says "taraḥtuhu" (I cast him); because the meaning of ṭarḥ is throwing, so he introduced the ba' for the sake of meaning, since the meaning is "they throw with the youth." This second opinion is, in my view, the more correct of the two, and the explanation of its like has been given in more than one place in this book, sufficiently so as to avoid repeating it here.

The people of ta'wil have said things similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of His words: ﴿you are hastening﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿some of what you are hastening for has drawn near to you﴾, he said: of the punishment.

**The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 27, verses 69–72**

**On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Say: Travel through the land and observe how was the end of the criminals﴾ (69) ﴿And do not grieve over them, and do not be in distress because of what they plot﴾ (70)**

God, dhikruhu, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to these deniers, concerning what I have brought you of the news from your Lord: ﴿Travel through the land and observe﴾ the abodes of those before you among the deniers of God's messengers, and their dwellings, how they are. Did God not ruin them and destroy their people for their denial of their messengers and their rejection of their sincere advice, so that the abodes were emptied of them and their traces and remains were effaced? That was the end of their criminality, and it is the custom of your Lord with everyone who follows their path in denying the messengers of their Lord. God will do the same to you if you do not hasten to repent of your disbelief and your denial of the messenger of your Lord.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And do not grieve over them﴾

God, dhikruhu, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Do not grieve over the turning away of these polytheists from you and their denial of you. ﴿And do not be in distress because of what they plot﴾, meaning: let your breast not be constricted by their scheming against you, for God is your helper against them, and will destroy them by the sword.

* *

**On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And they say, "When will this promise be, if you are truthful?" (71) Say, "Perhaps some of what you are hastening for has drawn near to you."﴾ (72)**

God, dhikruhu, says: The polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, who deny you concerning what you brought them from your Lord, say: ﴿When﴾ will ﴿this promise﴾ come, the promise you have made us of punishment, which, as you say, is upon us? ﴿If you are truthful﴾ in what you threaten us with. ﴿Say: "Perhaps﴾ it has drawn near to you" ﴿some of what you are hastening for﴾ of God's punishment. God, great is His majesty, says: Say to them, O Muhammad: perhaps it has come close to you and drawn near, ﴿some of what you are hastening for﴾ of God's punishment.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, i.e. exegesis) have said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ali related to me, saying: Abd Allah related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿Say: "Perhaps it has drawn near to you"﴾, that he said: it has come close to you.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿Say: "Perhaps some of what you are hastening for has drawn near to you"﴾, that he said: it has come close to you, some of what you are hastening for.

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿Perhaps it has drawn near to you﴾, he said: radifa: it has hastened upon you.

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿Say: "Perhaps some of what you are hastening for has drawn near to you"﴾, he said: it has come near.

- I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: ﴿has drawn near to you﴾: it has come close to you.

The grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyya) differed regarding the reason the lam enters in His words: ﴿radifa lakum﴾. The well-known usage of the Arabs is: radifahu amr, and aradafahu (something followed him), as one says: tabi'ahu and atba'ahu (he followed him). Some grammarians of Basra said: the lam is introduced here, thereby attaching the verb, as one says: ﴿for the dream you interpret﴾ and ﴿for their Lord they fear﴾.

Some grammarians of Kufa said: the lam is introduced here for the sake of meaning, because its meaning is: it drew near to them, as the poet said:

*"I said to her: the needs cast the youth about,*
*and they have wearied me, the mounts of their riding."*

[This is a half-line from the evidence cited by al-Farra' in (Ma'ani al-Qur'an, p. 236 of the Cairo University photographic edition), and its second half is: "and they have wearied me, the mounts of their riding." It is in (al-Lisan: ʿnā), and in its transmission the word is "ta'anahu" in place of "ta'annani". He said: 'ana al-shay' means he suffered it; one says 'anahu and ta'annahu, and ta'anna he. He said: "faqultu.." etc. The verse is evidence that the ba' in "bi-al-fata" is superfluous, like its use in His words (radifa lakum).]

So he introduced the ba' in "yatrahna" (they cast), although one says "taraḥtuhu" (I cast him); because the meaning of ṭarḥ is throwing, so he introduced the ba' for the sake of meaning, since the meaning is "they throw with the youth." This second opinion is, in my view, the more correct of the two, and the explanation of its like has been given in more than one place in this book, sufficiently so as to avoid repeating it here.

The people of ta'wil have said things similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of His words: ﴿you are hastening﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿some of what you are hastening for has drawn near to you﴾, he said: of the punishment.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verses 73–76:

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is full of bounty toward the people, but most of them do not give thanks (73). And indeed, your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they disclose (74).﴾

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, your Lord﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿is full of bounty toward the people﴾ by His leaving off hastening punishment upon them for their disobedience toward Him and their disbelief in Him; He is also a benefactor to them in that and in His other blessings upon them. ﴿But most of them do not give thanks﴾ ﴿for that﴾ bounty and favor of His toward them, so that they would devote worship sincerely to Him; rather, they associate with Him in worship what harms them and does not benefit them, and what has no bounty or favor toward them.

* *

And His words: ﴿And indeed, your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they disclose﴾

He says: And indeed your Lord knows the inner thoughts of the breasts of His creatures, the secrets of their souls, the hidden of their confidences, and the apparent matters of their open affairs; nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He keeps account of it against them, until He recompenses all of them with good for good and with the consequence of evil for evil.

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn related to me, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿And indeed, your Lord knows what their breasts conceal﴾: he said, "The secret."

* *

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And there is not an unseen thing in the heaven or earth but that it is in a clear register (75). Indeed, this Qur'an relates to the Children of Israel most of that over which they differ (76).﴾

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And there is not﴾ any hidden secret or concealed matter that is absent from the sight of observers ﴿in the heaven and the earth but that it is in a register﴾ — and this is the Mother of the Book, in which our Lord has recorded everything that exists from the beginning of His creation until the Day of Resurrection. By His words ﴿clear﴾ He means that it makes clear to whoever looks at it, and reads what our Lord, may His praise be exalted, has recorded in it.

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿And there is not an unseen thing in the heaven and earth but that it is in a clear register﴾: he said, "It means there is nothing in the heavens and earth, secret or open, but that He knows it."

* *

And His words: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an relates to the Children of Israel most of that over which they differ﴾

God, the Exalted, says: Indeed, this Qur'an that I have sent down to you, O Muhammad, relates to the Children of Israel the truth concerning most of the matters over which they differed, such as what they differed about regarding Jesus: the Jews said what they said about him, and the Christians said what they said about him, and because of their differing about him, these disowned those, and those disowned these, along with other matters over which they differed. So the Exalted said to them: Indeed, this Qur'an relates to you the truth concerning what you differed about, so follow it and acknowledge what is in it, for it relates to you with truth and guides you to the path of rectitude.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verse 77–78:

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And indeed, it is guidance and mercy for the believers. (77) Indeed, your Lord will judge between them by His ruling, and He is the Mighty, the Knowing. (78)﴾

His, may He be exalted and remembered, saying: Indeed, this Qur'an is guidance, meaning: a clarification from Allah, by which He makes clear the truth concerning what His creatures differ about in matters of their religion. ﴿And mercy for the believers﴾, meaning: and mercy for whoever affirms it as true and acts by what is in it. ﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them﴾, meaning: indeed, your Lord will judge between the disputing among the Children of Israel by His ruling concerning them, so He will take vengeance upon the wrongdoer among them, and will reward the good-doer among them who is in the right with his recompense. ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Knowing﴾, meaning: and your Lord is Mighty in His vengeance against the wrongdoer among them and among others; no one is able to prevent Him from taking vengeance when He takes it. The Knowing of the one in the right, the good-doer among these disputing Children of Israel concerning what they differed about, and among others, the wrongdoer who strays from guidance.

* *

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿So rely upon Allah. Indeed, you are upon the manifest truth. (79) Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away, retreating. (80)﴾

His, may He be exalted and remembered, saying to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: So entrust your affairs, O Muhammad, to Allah, and trust Him in them, for indeed He is sufficient for you. ﴿Indeed, you are upon the manifest truth﴾ for whoever contemplates it, reflects upon what is in it with his intellect, and ponders it with understanding, that it is the truth, unlike what the Jews and Christians, the disputing Children of Israel, are upon, and unlike what the people of idols are upon, who deny you regarding the truth that you have brought them. Meaning: do not let the denial of those who deny you, or the opposition of those who oppose you, grieve you, and proceed with the command of your Lord with which He sent you.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And you cannot guide the blind away from their misguidance. You can only make hear those who believe in Our verses, and they are Muslims﴾ (81). ﴿And when the word befalls them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth to speak to them that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs﴾ (82).

The reciters differed over the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Madina and Basra, and some of the Kufans, recited ﴿وَمَا أَنْتَ بِهَادِي﴾ (wa-ma anta bi-hadi) with a yā' and alif, and with the word "the blind" (al-'umy) in the genitive, meaning: you, O Muhammad, are not a guide of those who are blind to the truth ﴿عَنْ ضَلالَتِهِمْ﴾ (from their misguidance). The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited "وَمَا أنْتَ تَهْدِي العُمْيَ" with a tā' and "the blind" in the accusative, meaning: you do not guide them ﴿عَنْ ضَلالَتِهِمْ﴾ from their misguidance, but Allah guides them if He wills.

My view on this is that they are two readings close in meaning, both well known among the readers of the cities, so whichever of them the reciter reads is correct. The meaning of the speech is what I have described: ﴿وَمَا أَنْتَ﴾ (and you are not), O Muhammad, ﴿بِهادِي﴾ a guide of those whom Allah has blinded from guidance and rectitude, and has placed a veil over their sight, so that the path of rectitude is not made clear to them, turning them from their misguidance in which they are, to the way of rectitude and the path of right guidance.

* *

As for His words: ﴿إِنْ تُسْمِعُ إِلا مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ (You can only make hear those who believe in Our verses).

He says: you are not able to make anyone understand and comprehend the truth except one who hears from someone who believes in Our verses, meaning Our proofs, Our arguments, and the signs of Our revelation. ﴿فَهُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ (and they are Muslims): those will listen from you what you say, ponder it, reflect upon it and act upon it. They are the ones who hear.

Mention of those who said the same as what we have said regarding His words ﴿وَقَعَ﴾ (befalls)[[The author's commentary on the interpretation of verse 82 is missing here; the reports of the people of interpretation that follow indicate it.]]

Qatada, regarding His words ﴿وإذا وقع الْقَوْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, says: "when the word is due against them."

Mujahid, through Ibn Juraij, said: ﴿وَقَعَ الْقَوْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ "the punishment is right against them."

Ibn Juraij said: "the word" is the punishment.

Mention of those who said the same as what we have said regarding the meaning of "the word":

Qatada said: "the word" is the anger (al-ghadab).

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, from Ibn 'Ulayya, from Hisham, from Hafsa, who said: I asked Abu al-'Aliya about His words ﴿وَإِذَا وَقَعَ الْقَوْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, and he said: Allah revealed to Noah ﴿أَنَّهُ لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ مِنْ قَوْمِكَ إِلا مَنْ قَدْ آمَنَ﴾ (that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed). She said: It was as if a covering that was over my face was removed.

Some scholars said: the emergence of this creature is when people no longer enjoin good nor forbid evil.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb related to us, from al-Ash'ari, from Sufyan, from 'Amr ibn Qays, from 'Atiyya al-'Awfi, from Ibn 'Umar, regarding His words ﴿وَإِذَا وَقَعَ الْقَوْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ أَخْرَجْنَا لَهُمْ دَابَّةً مِنَ الأرْضِ﴾, he said: it is when they no longer enjoin good and forbid evil.

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan Abu al-Hasan, from 'Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i, from 'Atiyya, from Ibn 'Umar, regarding His words ﴿وَإِذَا وَقَعَ الْقَوْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ أَخْرَجْنَا لَهُمْ دَابَّةً مِنَ الأرْضِ﴾, he said: that is when enjoining good and forbidding evil are abandoned.

Ibn Bashshar related to us, from Abu Ahmad, from Sufyan, from 'Amr ibn Qays, from 'Atiyya, from Ibn 'Umar, regarding His words ﴿أَخْرَجْنَا لَهُمْ دَابَّةً مِنَ الأرْضِ تُكَلِّمُهُمْ﴾, he said: when they do not enjoin good and do not forbid evil.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr al-Maqdisi related to me, from Ash'ath ibn 'Abd Allah al-Sijistani, from Shu'ba, from 'Atiyya, regarding His words ﴿وإذا وقع القول عليهم أخرجنا لهم دابة من الأرض تُكَلِّمُهُمْ﴾, he said: when they do not recognise what is right and do not reject what is wrong.

It is mentioned that the earth from which the creature emerges is Makka.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb related to us, from al-Ash'ari, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from 'Atiyya, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: the creature emerges from a crack in al-Safa, like the running of a horse, for three days, and not a third of it has come out.

Ibn Humayd related to us, from al-Hakam ibn Bashir, from 'Amr ibn Qays, from al-Furat al-Qazzaz, from 'Amir ibn Wathila Abi al-Tufayl, from Hudhayfa ibn Usayd al-Ghifari, who said: When the creature emerges, some people will see it and say, "By Allah, we have seen the creature," until this reaches the ruler, who searches but cannot find anything. He said: Then it emerges and people see it, and they say, "By Allah, we have seen it," and this reaches the ruler, who searches but sees nothing, and he says: "Indeed, when the one who mentions it is ..." He said: until he counts the killing among it. He said: Then it emerges, and when people see it they enter the mosque to pray, and it comes to them and says: "Now you pray!" and it brands the disbeliever, and wipes a mark (ghurra) on the forehead of the Muslim. He said: The people will live for a time, one saying: "O believer," and another: "O disbeliever."

Al-Qasim related to us, from al-Husayn, from 'Uthman ibn Mattar, from Wasil, mawla of Abu 'Uyayna, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Hudhayfa, and Abu Sufyan related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qays ibn Sa'd, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Hudhayfa ibn Usayd, regarding His words ﴿أَخْرَجْنَا لَهُمْ دَابَّةً مِنَ الأرْضِ تُكَلِّمُهُمْ﴾, he said: The creature has three emergences: one emergence in some of the deserts, then it hides; and an emergence in some of the towns, when the rulers shed blood in it, then it hides. While people are at the most noble, greatest and most excellent of mosques, the earth lifts them up, and people flee in flight, and a group of believers remains, saying: "Nothing will save us from Allah." Then the creature emerges to them, making their faces shine like a shining star. Then it departs, and no seeker can catch it, nor can a fleeing one escape it. It comes to a man praying and says: "By Allah, you were not among the people of prayer," and he turns to it, and it brands him. He said: It makes the believer's face shine and brands the disbeliever. We said: What will people be on that day? He said: neighbours in dwellings, partners in wealth, and companions in journeys.

Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, from Ibn Fudayl, from al-Walid ibn Jumay', from 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Mughira, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Bayliani, from Ibn 'Umar: The people will spend the night travelling toward Jam', and the creature of the earth will spend the night travelling with them, and they will wake up having been branded by it from its head and tail. No believer will remain except it wipes him, and no disbeliever or hypocrite except it strikes him.

Mujahid ibn Musa related to us, from Yazid, from al-Khaybari, from Hayyan ibn 'Umayr, from Hassan ibn Hamsa, who said: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr say: If I wished, I would wear my two sandals and never touch the ground sitting until I stand upon the stones from between which the creature will emerge. And it is as if I see it having emerged in the wake of a caravan of pilgrims. He said: Whenever I performed the pilgrimage, I feared it would emerge behind us.

'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Amili related to us, from Abu Usama, from Hisham, from Qays ibn Sa'd, from 'Ata', who said: I saw 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, whose dwelling was near al-Safa, raise his foot while standing, and he said: If I wished, I would not set it down until I set it on the place from which the creature emerges.

'Isam ibn Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah related to us, from his father, from Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri, from Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, who said: I heard Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, and he mentioned the creature. Hudhayfa said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, from where will it emerge?" He said: "From the most sacred of mosques before Allah. While 'Isa is circumambulating the House with the Muslims, the earth will shake beneath them, like the shaking of a lamp, and al-Safa will split on the side near al-Mas'a, and the creature will emerge from al-Safa, first its head appears, polished, with fur and feathers. No seeker will overtake it, and no fleeing one will escape it. It brands people, believer and disbeliever. As for the believer, it leaves his face as if it were a shining star, and it writes between his eyes 'believer.' As for the disbeliever, it strikes between his eyes a black spot: 'disbeliever'."

Al-Qasim related to us, from al-Husayn, from Abu al-Husayn, from Hammad ibn Salama, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Aws ibn Khalid, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The creature will emerge with the seal of Sulayman and the staff of Musa. It will polish the face of the believer with the staff, and it will seal the nose of the disbeliever with the seal, so that when the people of a house gather, one says: 'O believer,' and another says: 'O disbeliever'."

He said: al-Husayn related to us, from Abu Sufyan, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, who said: It is a creature covered with down and feathers, having four legs, emerging from some valleys of Tihama. He said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: It will mark the face of the disbeliever with a black spot, which will spread over his face until his face turns black, and it will mark the face of the believer with a white spot, which will spread over his face until his face turns white. The people of a house will sit at the table and recognise the believer from the disbeliever, and they will trade in the markets and recognise the believer from the disbeliever.

Ibn 'Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi related to me, from Ibn Abi Maryam, from Ibn Lahi'a and Yahya ibn Ayyub, who both said: Ibn al-Hadi related to us, from 'Umar ibn al-Hakam, that he heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr say: The creature will emerge from a mountain pass, its head will touch the clouds while its feet are still in the earth, and it will pass by a person praying and say: "What has prayer to do with your need?" and it will brand him.

Salih ibn Misman related to us, from Ibn Abi Fudayk, from Yazid ibn 'Iyad, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, that it reached him from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The creature of the earth will emerge, and with it the seal of Sulayman and the staff of Musa. As for the disbeliever, it will seal him between his eyes with the seal of Sulayman, and as for the believer, it will wipe his face with the staff of Musa, and it will become white.

The reciters differed over the reading of His words ﴿تُكَلِّمُهُمْ﴾ (speaks to them). The majority of the reciters of the cities read it with a ḍamma on the tā' and a shadda on the lām, meaning: it informs them and tells them. Abu Za'ra ibn 'Amr read "تَكْلِمُهُمْ" with a fatha on the tā' and without shadda on the lām, meaning: it marks them.

The reading I do not permit anything other than is the reading of the majority of the reciters of the cities.

Those who spoke on interpretation said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

'Ali related to us, from Abu Salih, from Mu'awiya, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿أَخْرَجْنَا لَهُمْ دَابَّةً مِنَ الأرْضِ تُكَلِّمُهُمْ﴾, he said: it speaks to them.

Bishr related to us, from Yazid, from Sa'id, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿أَخْرَجْنَا لَهُمْ دَابَّةً مِنَ الأرْضِ تُكَلِّمُهُمْ﴾, and in some readings it is "تحدثهم" (informs them), saying to them: ﴿أن الناس كَانُوا بِآيَاتِنَا لا يُوقِنُونَ﴾ (that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs).

Al-Qasim related to us, from al-Husayn, from Hajjaj, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿تُكَلِّمُهُمْ﴾, he said: its speech informs them ﴿أَنَّ النَّاسَ كَانُوا بِآيَاتِنَا لا يُوقِنُونَ﴾.

* *

As for His words: ﴿أَنَّ النَّاسَ كَانُوا بِآيَاتِنَا لا يُوقِنُونَ﴾ (that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs):

The reciters differed over the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz, Basra and Syria read "إنَّ النَّاسَ" with a kasra on the alif of "inna," as a fresh statement giving information about the people, that they did not have certainty in the signs of Allah. Although it is kasra in the reading of these, the speech still applies to it. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of Basra read ﴿أَنَّ النَّاسَ كَانُوا﴾ with a fatha on the alif of "anna," meaning: it speaks to them that mankind..., so that it is in the accusative by the falling of the speech upon it.

The correct view on this is that they are two readings close in meaning, both widely transmitted among the readers of the cities, so whichever of them the reciter reads is correct.

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And you cannot guide the blind away from their misguidance. You can only make hear those who believe in Our verses, and they are Muslims﴾ (81). ﴿And when the word befalls them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth to speak to them that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs﴾ (82).

The reciters differed over the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Madina and Basra, and some of the Kufans, recited ﴿وَمَا أَنْتَ بِهَادِي﴾ (wa-ma anta bi-hadi) with a yā' and alif, and with the word "the blind" (al-'umy) in the genitive, meaning: you, O Muhammad, are not a guide of those who are blind to the truth ﴿عَنْ ضَلالَتِهِمْ﴾ (from their misguidance). The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited "وَمَا أنْتَ تَهْدِي العُمْيَ" with a tā' and "the blind" in the accusative, meaning: you do not guide them ﴿عَنْ ضَلالَتِهِمْ﴾ from their misguidance, but Allah guides them if He wills.

My view on this is that they are two readings close in meaning, both well known among the readers of the cities, so whichever of them the reciter reads is correct. The meaning of the speech is what I have described: ﴿وَمَا أَنْتَ﴾ (and you are not), O Muhammad, ﴿بِهادِي﴾ a guide of those whom Allah has blinded from guidance and rectitude, and has placed a veil over their sight, so that the path of rectitude is not made clear to them, turning them from their misguidance in which they are, to the way of rectitude and the path of right guidance.

* *

As for His words: ﴿إِنْ تُسْمِعُ إِلا مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ (You can only make hear those who believe in Our verses).

He says: you are not able to make anyone understand and comprehend the truth except one who hears from someone who believes in Our verses, meaning Our proofs, Our arguments, and the signs of Our revelation. ﴿فَهُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ (and they are Muslims): those will listen from you what you say, ponder it, reflect upon it and act upon it. They are the ones who hear.

It is mentioned that the earth from which the creature emerges is Makka.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb related to us, from al-Ash'ari, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from 'Atiyya, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: the creature emerges from a crack in al-Safa, like the running of a horse, for three days, and not a third of it has come out.

Ibn Humayd related to us, from al-Hakam ibn Bashir, from 'Amr ibn Qays, from al-Furat al-Qazzaz, from 'Amir ibn Wathila Abi al-Tufayl, from Hudhayfa ibn Usayd al-Ghifari, who said: When the creature emerges, some people will see it and say, "By Allah, we have seen the creature," until this reaches the ruler, who searches but cannot find anything. He said: Then it emerges and people see it, and they say, "By Allah, we have seen it," and this reaches the ruler, who searches but sees nothing, and he says: "Indeed, when the one who mentions it is ..." He said: until he counts the killing among it. He said: Then it emerges, and when people see it they enter the mosque to pray, and it comes to them and says: "Now you pray!" and it brands the disbeliever, and wipes a mark (ghurra) on the forehead of the Muslim. He said: The people will live for a time, one saying: "O believer," and another: "O disbeliever."

While people are at the most noble, greatest and most excellent of mosques, the earth lifts them up, and people flee in flight, and a group of believers remains, saying: "Nothing will save us from Allah." Then the creature emerges to them, making their faces shine like a shining star. Then it departs, and no seeker can catch it, nor can a fleeing one escape it. It comes to a man praying and says: "By Allah, you were not among the people of prayer," and he turns to it, and it brands him. He said: It makes the believer's face shine and brands the disbeliever. We said: What will people be on that day? He said: neighbours in dwellings, partners in wealth, and companions in journeys.

Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, from Ibn Fudayl, from al-Walid ibn Jumay', from 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Mughira, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Bayliani, from Ibn 'Umar: The people will spend the night travelling toward Jam', and the creature of the earth will spend the night travelling with them, and they will wake up having been branded by it from its head and tail. No believer will remain except it wipes him, and no disbeliever or hypocrite except it strikes him.

Mujahid ibn Musa related to us, from Yazid, from al-Khaybari, from Hayyan ibn 'Umayr, from Hassan ibn Hamsa, who said: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr say: If I wished, I would wear my two sandals and never touch the ground sitting until I stand upon the stones from between which the creature will emerge. And it is as if I see it having emerged in the wake of a caravan of pilgrims. He said: Whenever I performed the pilgrimage, I feared it would emerge behind us.

'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Amili related to us, from Abu Usama, from Hisham, from Qays ibn Sa'd, from 'Ata', who said: I saw 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, whose dwelling was near al-Safa, raise his foot while standing, and he said: If I wished, I would not set it down until I set it on the place from which the creature emerges.

'Isam ibn Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah related to us, from his father, from Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri, from Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, who said: I heard Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, and he mentioned the creature. Hudhayfa said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, from where will it emerge?" He said: "From the most sacred of mosques before Allah. While 'Isa is circumambulating the House with the Muslims, the earth will shake beneath them, like the shaking of a lamp, and al-Safa will split on the side near al-Mas'a, and the creature will emerge from al-Safa, first its head appears, polished, with fur and feathers. No seeker will overtake it, and no fleeing one will escape it. It brands people, believer and disbeliever. As for the believer, it leaves his face as if it were a shining star, and it writes between his eyes 'believer.' As for the disbeliever, it strikes between his eyes a black spot: 'disbeliever'."

Al-Qasim related to us, from al-Husayn, from Abu al-Husayn, from Hammad ibn Salama, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Aws ibn Khalid, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The creature will emerge with the seal of Sulayman and the staff of Musa. It will polish the face of the believer with the staff, and it will seal the nose of the disbeliever with the seal, so that when the people of a house gather, one says: 'O believer,' and another says: 'O disbeliever'."

He said: al-Husayn related to us, from Abu Sufyan, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, who said: It is a creature covered with down and feathers, having four legs, emerging from some valleys of Tihama. He said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: It will mark the face of the disbeliever with a black spot, which will spread over his face until his face turns black, and it will mark the face of the believer with a white spot, which will spread over his face until his face turns white. The people of a house will sit at the table and recognise the believer from the disbeliever, and they will trade in the markets and recognise the believer from the disbeliever.

Ibn 'Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi related to me, from Ibn Abi Maryam, from Ibn Lahi'a and Yahya ibn Ayyub, who both said: Ibn al-Hadi related to us, from 'Umar ibn al-Hakam, that he heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr say: The creature will emerge from a mountain pass, its head will touch the clouds while its feet are still in the earth, and it will pass by a person praying and say: "What has prayer to do with your need?" and it will brand him.

Salih ibn Misman related to us, from Ibn Abi Fudayk, from Yazid ibn 'Iyad, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, that it reached him from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The creature of the earth will emerge, and with it the seal of Sulayman and the staff of Musa. As for the disbeliever, it will seal him between his eyes with the seal of Sulayman, and as for the believer, it will wipe his face with the staff of Musa, and it will become white.

Mujahid ibn Musa related to us, from Yazid, from al-Khaybari, from Hayyan ibn 'Umayr, from Hassan ibn Hamsa, who said: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr say: If I wished, I would wear my two sandals and never touch the ground sitting until I stand upon the stones from between which the creature will emerge. And it is as if I see it having emerged in the wake of a caravan of pilgrims. He said: Whenever I performed the pilgrimage, I feared it would emerge behind us.

'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Amili related to us, from Abu Usama, from Hisham, from Qays ibn Sa'd, from 'Ata', who said: I saw 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, whose dwelling was near al-Safa, raise his foot while standing, and he said: If I wished, I would not set it down until I set it on the place from which the creature emerges.

'Isam ibn Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah related to us, from his father, from Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri, from Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, who said: I heard Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, and he mentioned the creature. Hudhayfa said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, from where will it emerge?" He said: "From the most sacred of mosques before Allah. While 'Isa is circumambulating the House with the Muslims, the earth will shake beneath them, like the shaking of a lamp, and al-Safa will split on the side near al-Mas'a, and the creature will emerge from al-Safa, first its head appears, polished, with fur and feathers. No seeker will overtake it, and no fleeing one will escape it. It brands people, believer and disbeliever. As for the believer, it leaves his face as if it were a shining star, and it writes between his eyes 'believer.' As for the disbeliever, it strikes between his eyes a black spot: 'disbeliever'."

Al-Qasim related to us, from al-Husayn, from Abu al-Husayn, from Hammad ibn Salama, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Aws ibn Khalid, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The creature will emerge with the seal of Sulayman and the staff of Musa. It will polish the face of the believer with the staff, and it will seal the nose of the disbeliever with the seal, so that when the people of a house gather, one says: 'O believer,' and another says: 'O disbeliever'."

He said: al-Husayn related to us, from Abu Sufyan, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, who said: It is a creature covered with down and feathers, having four legs, emerging from some valleys of Tihama. He said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: It will mark the face of the disbeliever with a black spot, which will spread over his face until his face turns black, and it will mark the face of the believer with a white spot, which will spread over his face until his face turns white. The people of a house will sit at the table and recognise the believer from the disbeliever, and they will trade in the markets and recognise the believer from the disbeliever.

Ibn 'Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi related to me, from Ibn Abi Maryam, from Ibn Lahi'a and Yahya ibn Ayyub, who both said: Ibn al-Hadi related to us, from 'Umar ibn al-Hakam, that he heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr say: The creature will emerge from a mountain pass, its head will touch the clouds while its feet are still in the earth, and it will pass by a person praying and say: "What has prayer to do with your need?" and it will brand him.

Salih ibn Misman related to us, from Ibn Abi Fudayk, from Yazid ibn 'Iyad, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, that it reached him from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The creature of the earth will emerge, and with it the seal of Sulayman and the staff of Musa. As for the disbeliever, it will seal him between his eyes with the seal of Sulayman, and as for the believer, it will wipe his face with the staff of Musa, and it will become white.

The reciters differed over the reading of His words ﴿تُكَلِّمُهُمْ﴾ (speaks to them). The majority of the reciters of the cities read it with a ḍamma on the tā' and a shadda on the lām, meaning: it informs them and tells them. Abu Za'ra ibn 'Amr read "تَكْلِمُهُمْ" with a fatha on the tā' and without shadda on the lām, meaning: it marks them.

The reading I do not permit anything other than is the reading of the majority of the reciters of the cities.

Those who spoke on interpretation said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

'Ali related to us, from Abu Salih, from Mu'awiya, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿أَخْرَجْنَا لَهُمْ دَابَّةً مِنَ الأرْضِ تُكَلِّمُهُمْ﴾, he said: it speaks to them.

Bishr related to us, from Yazid, from Sa'id, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿أَخْرَجْنَا لَهُمْ دَابَّةً مِنَ الأرْضِ تُكَلِّمُهُمْ﴾, and in some readings it is "تحدثهم" (informs them), saying to them: ﴿أن الناس كَانُوا بِآيَاتِنَا لا يُوقِنُونَ﴾ (that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs).

Al-Qasim related to us, from al-Husayn, from Hajjaj, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿تُكَلِّمُهُمْ﴾, he said: its speech informs them ﴿أَنَّ النَّاسَ كَانُوا بِآيَاتِنَا لا يُوقِنُونَ﴾.

* *

As for His words: ﴿أَنَّ النَّاسَ كَانُوا بِآيَاتِنَا لا يُوقِنُونَ﴾ (that mankind did not have certainty in Our signs):

The reciters differed over the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz, Basra and Syria read "إنَّ النَّاسَ" with a kasra on the alif of "inna," as a fresh statement giving information about the people, that they did not have certainty in the signs of Allah. Although it is kasra in the reading of these, the speech still applies to it. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of Basra read ﴿أَنَّ النَّاسَ كَانُوا﴾ with a fatha on the alif of "anna," meaning: it speaks to them that mankind..., so that it is in the accusative by the falling of the speech upon it.

The correct view on this is that they are two readings close in meaning, both widely transmitted among the readers of the cities, so whichever of them the reciter reads is correct.

The commentary on the verses: "And [mention] the Day when We gather from every nation a company [of those] who deny Our signs, and they will be driven on [in ranks] (83). Until, when they come, He will say: 'Did you deny My signs while you did not encompass them in knowledge? Or what was it that you used to do?' (84)"

Concerning the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And [mention] the Day when We gather from every nation a company [of those] who deny Our signs, and they will be driven on [in ranks]﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "And [mention] the Day when We gather from every generation (qarn) and religious community (milla) a company (fawj)," meaning a group of them and a troop, ﴿of those who deny Our signs﴾, meaning: of those who deny Our proofs and arguments. So He holds back the first of them until the last of them, so that all of them are assembled, and then they are driven to the Fire.

And in agreement with what we have said on this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And [mention] the Day when We gather from every nation a company [of those] who deny Our signs, and they will be driven on [in ranks]﴾ — he said: "It means: the Shi'a at the gathering."

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿a company from every nation﴾ — he said: "A troop."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿We gather from every nation a company﴾ — he said: "Troop after troop," ﴿so they will be driven on [in ranks]﴾.

- 'Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿of those who deny Our signs, and they will be driven on [in ranks]﴾ — he said: "He says: they will be pushed back."

- Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿so they will be driven on [in ranks]﴾ — he said: "Their first is held back until their last."

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿so they will be driven on [in ranks]﴾ — he said: "Guards who turn back the first of them to the last of them."

I have already explained the meaning of His saying ﴿yuza'un (they will be driven on)﴾ earlier, with its evidences, so that suffices and there is no need to repeat it in this place.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Until, when they come, He will say: "Did you deny My signs"﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verse 85–86:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And the word will fall upon them because they have wronged, so they will not speak﴾ [27:85]

He, the Exalted, says: The wrath and anger of God are due upon those who denied His signs, ﴿because they wronged﴾, meaning by their denial of God's signs, on the day they are gathered, ﴿so they will not speak﴾.

He says: they will not speak with a proof by which they can repel from themselves the magnitude of what has befallen them and the word that has fallen upon them.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Have they not seen that We made the night for them to rest therein﴾ [27:86]

He, the Exalted, says: Have these deniers of Our signs not seen Our alternation of the night and the day, and Our variation between them, by making this one a place of rest for them, in which they repose and are still, the ease of their bodies from the fatigue of moving about and turning in the day, and this one (the day) illuminated, in which they see things and observe them, so that they move about in it for their livelihoods, that they might reflect upon that and ponder, and know that the One who alternates these in this manner is the God whom nothing can overpower, and for whom it is not difficult to cause the living to die and to bring the dead back to life after death, just as it is not difficult for Him to make the day go and the night come, and the night go and the day come, with the difference of their conditions. ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe﴾.

He, the Exalted, says: Indeed, in Our making the night a place of rest and the day illuminated, there are evident proofs for a people who believe in God, of His power over what they believe in, namely the resurrection after death, and a proof for them of the oneness of God.
