Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verse 87:

The explanation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And on the Day the Horn is blown, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills. And all will come to Him, humbled.﴾ (27:87)

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And on the Day the Horn is blown﴾. We have already mentioned their differences in what has passed, and we clarified the correct view on this matter with its evidences. However, we will mention in this place some of the reports that were not mentioned there. Some of them said: it is a horn that is blown into.

Mention of some reports not mentioned previously concerning this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And on the Day the Horn is blown﴾, he said: "Like the shape of a trumpet."

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: "The Sur: the trumpet." He said: "It is a trumpet. Its holder takes hold of it, gripping it with his two hands on the edge of the horn, between its edge and its mouth about the measure of a handful or so. He has knelt on the knee of one of his legs, then he gestured and knelt on the knee of his left leg, crouching on its foot, its heel beneath his thigh and buttock, and the tips of its toes in the dust."

⁕ He said: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah, who said: "The Sur is like the shape of a horn, one of its knees raised toward the sky and the other lowered. He has not closed the lids of his eyes in sleep since Allah created the heavens, ready and attentive, having placed the Sur on his mouth, waiting for when he is commanded to blow into it."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Ismail ibn Rafi al-Madani, from Yazid ibn Ziyad — Abu Ja'far said: "and the correct is: Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad" — from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayrah: that he said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the Sur?" He said: "A horn." He said: "And what is it like?" He said: "A great horn into which three blasts will be blown. The first: the blast of terror (nafkhat al-faza'), the second: the blast of swooning (nafkhat al-sa'q), and the third: the blast of rising to the Lord of the worlds (nafkhat al-qiyam). Allah will command Israfil with the first blast, saying: 'Blow the blast of terror.' So he will blow the blast of terror, and the people of the heavens and the people of the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills. Allah will command him, and he will prolong it and extend it, and it will not cease. This is what Allah means when He says: ﴿And these do not await but a single cry, for which there is no reversal﴾. Then Allah will set the mountains in motion, and they will become like mirages, and the earth will be shaken with its inhabitants with a violent shaking. This is what Allah means when He says: ﴿On the Day the quaking one quakes, followed by the following one; hearts that Day will be trembling﴾. The earth will be like a ship moored in the sea, struck by the waves, capsized with its people, or like a lamp hung from a cord, swayed by the winds, and people will sway upon its back. Nursing mothers will be distracted, pregnant women will give birth, children will turn gray, and devils will fly away fleeing until they reach the horizons, where the angels will meet them and strike their faces, and they will turn back. People will turn their backs fleeing, calling out to one another. This is what Allah means when He says: ﴿The Day of Calling Out, the Day you turn your backs fleeing; you will have no protector from Allah; and whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾. While they are in that state, the earth will split from one side to the other, and they will see a great matter, and such distress will seize them that only Allah knows its extent. Then they will look at the sky, and behold, it will be like molten brass. Then its sun and moon will be eclipsed, its stars will be scattered, and then it will be stripped away from them."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "And the dead know nothing of any of that." Abu Hurayrah said: "O Messenger of Allah, then who is excluded by Allah when He says: ﴿so whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills﴾?" He said: "Those are the martyrs. Terror only reaches the living. Those are alive with their Lord, receiving provision. Allah protects them from the terror of that Day and secures them, and it is the punishment of Allah which He sends upon the worst of His creation."

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ismail ibn Rafi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah, Blessed and Exalted, finished with the heavens and the earth, He created the Sur and gave it to an angel, who places it on his mouth, gazing with his eyes toward the Throne, waiting for when he will be commanded." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, and what is the Sur?" He said: "A horn." I said: "And what is it like?" He said: "Great. By Him in whose hand is my soul, the circumference of its circle is like the breadth of the heavens and the earth. He will command it, and he will blow the blast of terror, and the people of the heavens and the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills." Then he mentioned the rest of the hadith similar to the hadith of Abu Kurayb from al-Muharibi, except that in his narration he said "like a ship anchored in the sea."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: and it is blown into the trumpet of creation (sur al-khalq).

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿On the Day the Horn is blown﴾, that is, into the creation.

* *

His words: ﴿so whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified﴾

He says: whoever is in the heavens of the angels and whoever is on the earth of jinn, humans and devils will be terrified, from the horror of what they witness on that Day.

If someone says: How is it said ﴿fa-fazi'a﴾ (and so terrified), making the verb "fazi'a" (past) connected to "yunfakhu" (present), which is yaf'alu? It is said: The Arabs do this in places where "idha" (when) is suitable, because "idha" can take either the past or present verb, as in your saying: "I will visit you when you visited me," and "I will visit you when you visit me." So when "yawm" (day) is placed in the position of "idha," it takes its role. If it is said: Where is the answer to His words: ﴿And on the Day the Horn is blown, so terrified﴾? It is said: It is permissible that it be implied with the "wa" (and), as if it were said: "And the word will fall upon them for what they wronged, so they will not speak, and that is the day the Horn is blown." And it is permissible that it be omitted, relying on the indication of the discourse upon it, as it is said: ﴿And if only those who did wrong could see﴾, its answer being omitted.

* *

His words: ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾

It was said: those whom Allah excepted in this place from being struck by terror on that Day are the martyrs, since they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision, even though they are counted among the dead in the view of the people of the world. This is what has come in the report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which we mentioned in the previous report.

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: al-Awwam informed us, from one who narrated to him, from Abu Hurayrah, that he recited this verse: ﴿so whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills﴾, and said: "They are the martyrs."

* *

His words: ﴿And all will come to Him, humbled﴾

He says: And all will come to Him, submissive and abased.

In agreement with what we have said on this, the people of interpretation said.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And all will come to Him, humbled﴾, he says: "Submissive."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And all will come to Him, humbled﴾, he said: "Submissive."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And all will come to Him, humbled﴾, he said: "The humbled (dakhir) is the submissive, the abased. For the person who is frightened, when he is frightened, his only concern is to flee from the matter he fears. So when the Horn is blown, they will be terrified, and there will be no escape for them from Allah."

The readers differed in reading His words: ﴿And all will come to Him, humbled﴾. The majority of readers in the cities recited it as "wa-kullun atawhu" with the alif of "ataw" extended, on the pattern of "fa'iluhu" (fa'ilu-hu). [[Ataw: plural of ati, on the pattern of fa'il. Its original form was ātiyūhu; the damma was transferred from the yā' to the tā' because of its heaviness, then the yā' was dropped because it was silent and the following wāw was silent, so it became ātūhu on the pattern of fā'ilūhu. Its pattern before dropping the yā' was fā'ilūhu, which is what the author intended.]] except Ibn Mas'ud, who recited it as "wa-kullun atuhu" on the pattern of "fa'aluhu," and the later readers al-A'mash and Hamzah followed him in that reading. Those who read in the pattern of "fa'ilu" argued on the consensus of the readers on His words: ﴿And all of them will come to Him individually﴾ (19:95, wa-kulluhum ati-hi). They said: so likewise His words "ataw-hu" in the plural. As for those who read according to the reading of Abdullah, they referred it to His words: ﴿fa-fazi'a﴾ (so terrified), as if they directed the meaning of the discourse to: "And on the Day the Horn is blown, so terrified are those in the heavens and those on the earth, and they all came to Him humbled," just as it is said in speech: "He saw, and he fled, and he returned, and he was humbled."

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that they are two readings widely transmitted among the readers of the cities, and their meanings are close; so whichever of the two a reader recites, he is correct.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verse 88:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them rigid, while they pass by as the passing of clouds — the handiwork of Allah, who has perfected everything. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what you do.﴾

Allah, He is exalted in remembrance, says: ﴿And you see the mountains﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿thinking them﴾ standing still, ﴿while they pass by﴾.

Like the statement of:

* Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them rigid﴾ — he said: standing still. And it was only said: ﴿while they pass by as the passing of clouds﴾ because they gather and then move, so the one who sees them thinks, because of their great mass, that they are stationary, while they are moving with swift motion, as the poet al-Ja'di said:

With a host like a mountain, you would think them / standing still for pilgrims, while the riding camels trot along. [[Al-Ara'an: he means by it a great army; he likened it to a huge mountain with its projecting spurs (al-ra'an), which are the extremities, like the spurs of mountains. Al-Ra'an is the great prominent part of a mountain that you see projecting forward. It was also said al-Ara'an is one that is agitated by its multitude. Al-Tawd: the great mountain. Al-Hajj: plural of hajah. Tuhamlij: walks with the hamlaja, and the hamlaja is a good gait with speed. The verse is evidence that a massive thing, which you see moving, you think to be still, although it is moving very swiftly, as with the march of an army, or the sailing of a ship on the sea, which the onlooker thinks is standing still while it is speeding along. That is the condition of the mountains at the Resurrection: you see them as though rigid, while they move swiftly like clouds.]]

* * *

His saying: ﴿the handiwork of Allah, who has perfected everything﴾

— and made His creation firmly fashioned.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:

* Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿the handiwork of Allah, who has perfected everything﴾ — he said: He made everything firm.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿the handiwork of Allah, who has perfected everything﴾ — he said: He made beautiful everything He created and made it firm.

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Who has perfected everything﴾ — he said: He made everything firm and arranged it.

* al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid: ﴿perfected﴾ — made firm.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Indeed, He is Acquainted with what you do﴾ — He, exalted in remembrance, says: Indeed Allah has knowledge and awareness of what His servants do of good and evil, of obedience to Him and disobedience, and He will recompense all of them for all of that: good for good, and evil with its like.

**The explanation of His the Exalted's words:** ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, he will have better than it, and they will be safe from the terror of that Day. And whoever comes with an evil deed, their faces will be overturned into the Fire. Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?﴾ (27:89–90)

His the Exalted's words mean: Whoever comes (before God) with His Oneness and faith in Him, and the statement "There is no god but God," with certainty in his heart, ﴿he will have﴾ from this good deed with God ﴿better﴾ on the Day of Resurrection. That better reward is that God will reward him ﴿with﴾ Paradise, ﴿and will keep him safe from the terror﴾ of the Great Blast, which is the blowing of the Trumpet. ﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed﴾ means: whoever comes, on the Day he meets Him, with associating partners with Him and denying His oneness, ﴿their faces will be overturned into the Fire﴾ of Hell.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation, i.e. the early exegetes) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani related to me, saying: al-Fadl ibn Dukayn related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Ayyub al-Bajali related to us, saying: I heard Abu Zur'a say: Abu Hurayra said – Yahya said: "I think he related it from the Prophet (ﷺ)": "﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, he will have better than it, and they will be safe from the terror of that Day﴾," he said: "It is 'There is no god but God.'" "﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed, their faces will be overturned into the Fire﴾," he said: "It is associating partners (with God)."

- Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi related to us, saying: Abu Yahya al-Hammani related to us, from al-Nadr ibn Arabi, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: "﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, he will have better than it, and they will be safe from the terror of that Day﴾," he said: "Whoever comes with 'There is no god but God.'" "﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed, their faces will be overturned into the Fire﴾," he said: "With associating partners."

- Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, His words: "﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, he will have better than it﴾," he said: "Whoever comes with 'There is no god but God.'" "﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed﴾," which is associating partners.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, His words: "﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed﴾," he said: "With associating partners."

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, His words: "﴿Whoever comes with a good deed﴾," he said: "The word of sincerity (al-ikhlas)." "﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed﴾," he said: "Associating partners."

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly. Ibn Jurayj said: I heard Ata say about it: associating partners, meaning in His words: "﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed﴾."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Abu al-Mahjal, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ibrahim, who said: he used to swear without making an exception that "﴿Whoever comes with a good deed﴾" is "There is no god but God," and "﴿Whoever comes with an evil deed﴾" is associating partners.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Abd al-Malik, from Ata, similarly.

- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, saying: Musa ibn Ubayda related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b: "﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed, their faces will be overturned into the Fire﴾," he said: "Associating partners."

- Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Hafs related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Sa'id related to us, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, who was a man who fought often in the holy war, who said: While he was in some of his solitude, he raised his voice: "There is no god but God alone, without partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the praise; He gives life and causes death; in His hand is the good, and He is over all things capable." He said: A man replied to him: "What are you saying, servant of God?" He said: "I say what you hear." He said: "Indeed, this is the word that God mentioned: '﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, he will have better than it, and they will be safe from the terror of that Day﴾.'"

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: "﴿Whoever comes with a good deed﴾," he said: "Sincerity (al-ikhlas)." "﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed﴾," he said: "Associating partners."

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words: "﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed﴾," meaning: associating partners.

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Abu Sufyan related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan: "﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed﴾," he says: associating partners.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed, their faces will be overturned into the Fire﴾," he said: "The evil deed: associating partners, disbelief."

- Sa'd ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam related to me, saying: Hafs ibn Umar al-Adani related to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Aban related to us, from Ikrima, regarding His words: "﴿Whoever comes with a good deed﴾," he said: "The testimony that there is no god but God." "﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed﴾," he said: "The evil deed: associating partners." al-Hakam said: Ikrima said: "Everything in the Qur'an called an evil deed (sayyi'a) is associating partners."

Those who explained His words "﴿he will have better than it﴾" said the same as what we have said.

Those who said this:

- Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: "﴿he will have better than it﴾," so from it the good reaches him, meaning: from the good deed, good reaches the one who brought it. Ibn Abbas meant by this: from the good deed, good reaches the one who came with it.

- Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Rawh ibn Ubada related to us, saying: Husayn al-Shahid related to us, from al-Hasan: "﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, he will have better than it﴾," he said: "He will have from it (a share)."

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Abu Sufyan related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, who said: Whoever comes with "There is no god but God," he will have better than it, better.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, His words: "﴿he has better than it﴾," he says: he has a portion of it.

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, he will have better than it﴾," he said: he has good from it. As for whether it is better than faith, no; but he has good from it, he obtains some good from it.

- Sa'd ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam related to us, saying: Hafs ibn Umar related to us, saying: al-Hakam related to us, from Ikrima, His words: "﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, he will have better than it﴾," he said: Nothing is better than "There is no god but God," but he has good from it.

Ibn Zayd used to say about this:

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: "﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, he will have better than it﴾," he said: God gives him ten for one, and this is better than it.

The readers (al-qurra') differed in reading His words: "﴿and they will be safe from the terror of that Day﴾." Some readers of Basra read it: "wa-hum min fazaʿi yawma'idhin aminun," with fazaʿ annexed to yawm. A group of the readers of Kufa read: "min fazaʿin yawma'idhin," with fazaʿ in tanwin (indefinite).

The correct view on this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings in the recitation of the cities (al-amsar), close in meaning; whichever of them the reciter reads is correct. However, the annexed form is more pleasing to me, because the terror is a known one. When this is so, it is definite, given the context of His words: "﴿And on the Day when the Trumpet is blown, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except whom God wills﴾" (27:87). When this is so, it is clear that by His words "﴿and they will be safe from the terror of that Day﴾" He meant the terror that was mentioned before it. When this is so, it is undoubtedly definite, and annexation, when it is definite, is preferable to omitting the annexation. Another reason: when it is annexed, it is clearer as a report of their safety from all the horrors of that Day; whereas if it is not annexed, the more likely meaning is that safety is granted from some of its horrors.

As for His words: "﴿Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?﴾"

His the Exalted's words mean: It is said to them: "Are you, O polytheists, recompensed except for what you used to do," when God has overturned your faces into the Fire, and except for the recompense of what you used to do in the world, of things that anger your Lord. The phrase "it is said to them" is omitted, being sufficiently indicated by the context.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 27, verse 91:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, I have been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, who has made it sacred, and to Him belongs everything. And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims﴾ (27:91).

Exalted is He, mentioning His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), says: O Muhammad, say: ﴿Indeed, I have been commanded to worship the Lord of this city﴾, meaning Makkah, ﴿who has made it sacred﴾ for His creation, that they shed blood in it unlawfully, or wrong anyone in it, or hunt its game, or cut its grass, apart from the idols that you worship, O polytheists.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, I have been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, who has made it sacred﴾, meaning: Makkah.

And His saying: ﴿and to Him belongs everything﴾

That is, the Lord of this city owns all things as a possession. So it is to Him that I have been commanded to worship, not to one who owns nothing. Exalted is His praise, He mentioned ﴿the Lord of this city, who has made it sacred﴾ and singled it out from among the other cities, though He is the Lord of all lands, because He intended to make the polytheists of the people of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who are the people of Makkah, aware of His blessing upon them and His kindness to them, and that the One whom they ought to worship is the One who made their land sacred and kept people away from them, while in the rest of the lands some of them devour others and kill others. He is not one who had no favour bestowed upon them, nor one who is able to bring them benefit or harm.

And His saying: ﴿And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims﴾

That is: my Lord has commanded me to submit my face to Him as a hanif, so that I may be among the Muslims who adhere to the religion of His intimate friend Ibrahim and your forefather, O polytheists, not among those who oppose the rightly guided religion of their forefather and follow the religion of Iblis, the enemy of Allah.

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And to recite the Qur'an. Whoever is guided, is only guided for his own soul; and whoever goes astray, say: "I am only one of the warners."﴾ (92)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿Say: "I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city"﴾ and ﴿"to be among those who submit"﴾, ﴿"and to recite the Qur'an."﴾ ﴿Whoever is guided﴾ means: whoever follows me, believes in me and in what I have brought, and takes the path of right guidance. ﴿Then he is only guided for his own soul﴾ means: whoever follows the right course by following me, believing in me and in what I have brought, does so for his own soul, for by his belief in me and in what I have brought he is safe from My vengeance in this world and from My punishment in the Hereafter.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And whoever goes astray﴾

That means: whoever deviates from the straight path by denying me and what I have brought from God. ﴿Then say: "I am only one of the warners."﴾ He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Say, O Muhammad, to whoever has gone astray from the straight path, denied you, and did not believe in what I have brought from Me: "I am only one of those who warn their people of God's punishment and His wrath for their disobedience to Him. I have warned you of this, O company of the disbelievers of Quraysh. If you accept and desist from what God dislikes from you, namely associating others with Him, you will obtain your own portion. If you reject and deny, you have only harmed yourselves. I have conveyed to you what I was commanded to convey, and I have advised you."

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And say: "Praise be to God. He will show you His signs, and you will recognise them. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do."﴾ (93)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to those polytheists of your people who say to you: ﴿"When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾: ﴿"Praise be to God"﴾ for His blessing upon us by guiding us to the truth from which you are blind. ﴿He will show you your Lord's signs of His punishment and wrath, and you will recognise through them the truth of my counsel to you, and the truth of what I have called you to of right guidance will become clear.﴾

And the interpretation of those who interpret (the Qur'an) has said the like of what we have said in this regard.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿He will show you His signs, and you will recognise them﴾: He said: "In yourselves, and in the heavens and the earth, and in provision."

al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿He will show you His signs, and you will recognise them﴾: He said: "In yourselves, and the heavens and the earth, and provision."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what you do﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And your Lord, O Muhammad, is not unaware of what these polytheists do. But for them there is an appointed term which they will surely reach; when they reach it, they will not delay by an hour nor advance by an hour. He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet (ﷺ): So do not let their denial of you grieve you, for I am behind their destruction, and I am lying in wait for them. So be certain for yourself of victory, and for your enemy of humiliation and disgrace.

End of the commentary on Surah an-Naml.

To God belongs all praise and grace, and in Him is trust and protection.

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And to recite the Qur'an. Whoever is guided, is only guided for his own soul; and whoever goes astray, say: "I am only one of the warners."﴾ (92)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿Say: "I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city"﴾ and ﴿"to be among those who submit"﴾, ﴿"and to recite the Qur'an."﴾ ﴿Whoever is guided﴾ means: whoever follows me, believes in me and in what I have brought, and takes the path of right guidance. ﴿Then he is only guided for his own soul﴾ means: whoever follows the right course by following me, believing in me and in what I have brought, does so for his own soul, for by his belief in me and in what I have brought he is safe from My vengeance in this world and from My punishment in the Hereafter.
